01 - Overview

Seven journeys across three lighthouses

Executive summary

In the three journeys mapped so far, complaints climb after the purchase. They run 28% to 34% while people choose, and 48% to 60% once the product is in use and needs fixing.

WHERE IT HURTS
Products that fail in use cause the most pain in every journey.
Product failures lead in all three journeys when we count the people who raise them. That is 476 people in Journey 1, 2,382 in Journey 2 and 1,050 in Journey 3. Knowledge gaps come second in each, at 361, 349 and 447.
WHAT THE SHELF COVERS
The range reaches most steps, and own-brand share varies by journey.
The range serves 82 of 99 sub-steps. Own brand makes up 2% of products in Journey 1, 36% in Journey 2 and 41% in Journey 3. It is strong in manual tools and consumables, and it has the most room to grow in powered equipment and structures.
WHERE TO ACT
Most moves use products that already exist.
The finelines hold 125 gap opportunities, 100 fixes, 78 chances to say it better and 37 chances to speak louder. The Opportunities tab brings them together with the territories and the roadmap.
The lighthouses and the seven journeysSeven journeys sit under the three lighthouses. We have mapped three of them. The other four will follow using the same method.

Canadian Tire defines the three lighthouses. The first is maintaining my outdoor space and garden, such as watering plants or cleaning the pool. The second is cleaning the exterior of my living space and yard, such as raking leaves, shovelling snow or power washing. The third is preparing my outdoor space and garden, such as building a shed or planting vegetables. The lighthouse labels for Journeys 4 to 7 are our proposal.

What runs across the journeysFive patterns hold in more than one journey. The tabs that follow cover each one in detail.
  • The pain comes after the sale. In Journeys 1, 2 and 3, complaints run 29%, 28% and 34% while people choose. They rise to 48%, 60% and 60% while people watch, fix and replace. The opening is in products that hold up, with parts on hand when they break.
  • Failing products cause the most pain, and knowledge gaps come second. Both hold in all three journeys when we count the people who raise them. Knowledge gaps make up 170 of the 742 pain points. These people don't know when to act, how much to use or which product to choose. Many of these questions can be answered on the label, the shelf or the product page.
  • Own brand leads in simple products and has room to grow in powered ones. Yardworks, Aquarius and Certified hold manual snow tools, pool chemicals and snowblower parts. National brands hold the best tier in powered equipment and in almost everything with a motor, a battery or a frame. The Brands tab has the detail.
  • Forum buyers watch for event prices. In Journey 2, 27 comments describe timing purchases to points events, and 73 describe price matching. The value comparisons show Canadian Tire ahead on big-ticket machines. They show it behind on consumables that people buy several times a season. The Value tab has the detail.
  • Domestic supply favours bulky, simple products. In Journey 1, 65% of products are made in Canada or the US, led by peat and seed. The share is 27% in Journey 2 and 15% in Journey 3. Shovels, ice melt, frost cloth, balancers and hard-sided hot tubs have the strongest case for domestic supply. The Sourcing tab has the detail.
How to read this briefThe Journeys tab answers everything for one journey at a time. The tabs after it look across journeys.
  • Journeys has a picker for each journey. Each journey opens with the findings. The interactive map comes next and shows pain points, hacks and finelines at every step. The evidence follows, covering the three questions, the journey itself and the opportunities, which include fineline opportunities and territories.
  • Value, Brands and Sourcing answer the three questions across journeys. Opportunities brings every territory, fineline opportunity and roadmap move together. Method says how the evidence was gathered and what it can and can't tell you.
  • Every pain point is a hypothesis from secondary research, ready to test with real customers. The numbers are counts of the comments we read. They do not measure market share.

WHERE IT HURTS
Fixing failed gear and watching seedlings draw the most complaints.
The fix-the-gear step draws 70% complaints, and watching the seedlings draws 59%. Both steps come after the sale. Complaints means the share of comments that are negative, with mixed comments counted as half.
WHAT THE SHELF COVERS
The range covers seed starting, lights and greenhouses, and the opening is frost protection and season extension.
We found no frost cloth, row cover, cold frame, cloche or hoop kit at Canadian Tire. Winter shrub covers are sold on canadiantire.ca but don't appear in the Category Review.
VALUE, BRANDS, SOURCING
Prices hold up on big items and trail on refills, and own brand has almost no presence in this journey.
Domestic manufacturing is strongest in bulky outdoor gear. The evidence below answers all three questions first, each with its limits.
How to read this: each column is a step in the job. Sub-steps are what people do at that step. Pain points are what goes wrong, written from the comments. Thin evidence means fewer than 5 entries. Border colour: coral is pain share 0.50 or higher, gold 0.30 to 0.49, grey 0.15 to 0.29, green below 0.15.

The three questions
This section answers the three questions for this journey: value against other retailers, brand architecture and domestic manufacturing.
Q1 - Value against other retailersThe question“How does our value proposition compare to key competitors (brands and retailers)?”On identical items, Canadian Tire wins the first purchase and other retailers win the refills. Big-ticket items hold up on price. Season-extension gear is sold at other retailers, which makes it an opening here.
What to do
Buying
Reprice Jiffy refills to match Home Depot and Walmart. Returning growers pay more here for the parts they buy again. The dome is C$2.99 against C$2.48, and 13.2 L of Jiffy mix is C$9.99 against C$7.45.
5 people on the 1 pain card this answers, 2% of the 325 people commenting on this sub-step. Read the comments
Buying
Add 72 and 200 count pellet refill packs. Canadian Tire sells pellet refills in packs of 36, at C$0.18 a pellet. Rivals sell 72 and 200 counts at C$0.11 to 0.17 a pellet.
5 people on the 1 pain card this answers, 2% of the 325 people commenting on this sub-step. Read the comments
Sourcing and vendors
Ask a vendor for sharper Jiffy Hydro pricing. The Jiffy heat mat is C$44.99 here and C$37.97 at Walmart, and the Hydro line runs 17 to 19% higher. Generic mats sell for C$17 to 24.Rests on price gap vs Walmart and generic mats, not on a count of people.
Product development
Spec a heavier Garden Club tray to lift its rating. Garden Club seed starting sits 70% below national brands at the better level, with medians across different products. It rates 4.07 from 258 ratings, against 4.38 from 646 for national brands.
30 people on the 3 pain cards this answers, 5% of the 587 people commenting on these 3 sub-steps. Read the comments

Shares are of the comments we read, not of customers or sales. One person on two cards counts once.

Limits: we checked prices on 20 October 2026, in the off-season, from Home Depot, Walmart and Lee Valley pages. Amazon.ca blocked automated reading, and RONA and Costco showed no prices, so the ranges leave them out. Several competitor items were out of stock.

  • Same kit, dearer refills. The McKenzie with Jiffy 72-pellet kit costs C$18.99 at Canadian Tire, C$19.48 at Home Depot and C$19.49 at Walmart. The parts a returning grower buys again cost more here. The dome is C$2.99 against C$2.48, and the Pro-Hex tray is C$8.99 against C$7.48 to 8.47. The 36-pellet refill is C$6.49 against C$5.98, and 13.2 L of Jiffy mix is C$9.99 against C$7.45.
  • Jiffy Hydro costs 17 to 19% more than at Walmart. The heat mat is C$44.99 against C$37.97, and the light and stand is C$69.99 against C$59.97. Generic mats sell for C$17 to 24.
  • Big-ticket items hold their price. The Palram Hybrid 6 x 8 sells for C$1,249.99, against C$1,298 at Home Depot. Price pressure comes from cheaper models, such as an 8 x 6 at C$369.99 at Walmart. Competitors aren't selling the same model for less.
  • Pack sizes. Canadian Tire sells pellet refills only in packs of 36, at C$0.18 a pellet. Competitors sell counts of 72 and 200 at C$0.11 to 0.17 a pellet.
  • Room to grow in season extension. Other retailers sell frost cloth at C$10.99 to 28.99, cold frames at C$65 to 379, hoop kits at C$34 to 100 and heat mat thermostats at about C$40. Lee Valley carries all four.

Q2 - Brand architecture across good, better, bestThe question“Do we have the right brand architecture and assortment mix, and are our brands positioned appropriately across the Good-Better-Best spectrum?”Own brand appears in one of the journey's seven finelines, at a single tier. Customers see it under the Jiffy name. NOMA holds the strongest own-brand position in the journey, and it sits outside the product list Canadian Tire shared.
What to do
Brand and marketing
Rename the Jiffy listed tray and dome as Garden Club. The canadiantire.ca site lists both Garden Club items under the Jiffy name. 76 people want rigid trays and fitted domes, so the brand they already buy should carry its own name.
69 people on the 8 pain cards this answers, 7% of the 996 people commenting on these 5 sub-steps. Read the comments
Buying
Move NOMA T5 strips and bulbs into the seed bay. NOMA grow lights rate 4.4 to 4.6 stars on 77 to 137 reviews and sit outside Seasonal and Gardening. 18 people report early light failures, with NOMA named most, so run burn in tests first.Rests on rating and range placement, not on a count of people.
Buying
Add products for frost timing and greenhouse venting. The range has 0 products where 47 people raise weather pains and 46 raise frost date pains. Greenhouse heat and venting has 2 products against 53 people, an opening for J1-T4 and J1-T6.
62 people on the 8 pain cards this answers, 10% of the 595 people commenting on these 6 sub-steps. Read the comments
Buying
Reprice seed packets and mixes so each level steps up. Better seed packets cost more than best, at medians of C$12.99 and C$10.49. Good and best seed starting mix share a C$10.99 median, and some of these tiers are our estimate from price.
5 people on the 1 pain card this answers, 2% of the 325 people commenting on this sub-step. Read the comments

Shares are of the comments we read, not of customers or sales. One person on two cards counts once.

Limits: the brand placement list Canadian Tire shared gives tiers by brand within each fineline. Where a brand holds several tiers, we split its products across them in price order and marked those tiers as estimates. A tier for each product would confirm them.

  • One own-brand position. Garden Club makes a seed tray with a dome at the better tier, and canadiantire.ca lists it under the Jiffy name. The good and best tiers are open for own brand across the journey.
  • NOMA grow lights are Canadian Tire's own brand, and customers rate the bulbs and T5 strips 4.4 to 4.6 stars on 77 to 137 reviews each. They're sold outside Seasonal and Gardening.
  • Grow lights come from one supplier. SunBlaster and Jump Start are both Hydrofarm brands.
  • Tiers that don't follow price. Better seed packets cost more than best ones, at medians of C$12.99 and C$10.49. Good and best seed-starting mix share a C$10.99 median. Canadian Tire carries one heat mat, at the best tier, for C$44.99.
  • Tiers mix product types. In greenhouses, the good tier holds walk-ins at a C$785 median. The better tier includes C$60 mini greenhouses. Read the ladder by product type.

Q3 - Domestic manufacturing and sourcingThe question“Are there any whitespace opportunities or priority categories where domestic manufacturing is particularly strong and could present additional development potential?”The strongest domestic options in this journey are bulky outdoor gear: frost cloth and row cover, cold frames and hoop kits, and walk-in greenhouses. Indoor electronics and coir favour overseas supply.
What to do
Sourcing and vendors
Source frost cloth and row cover from Ontario fabric. Spunbond fabric is made in North Bay, Ontario, and cutting and packing for retail needs little capital. The range has no frost cloth yet, which leaves J1-T5 open at frost cover.
5 people on the 1 pain card this answers, 2% of the 271 people commenting on these 3 sub-steps. Read the comments
Product development
Spec an own brand cold frame and hoop kit. Cold frame inputs are domestic, and no Canadian retail brand is on the shelf. Rivals sell cold frames at C$65 to 379 and hoop kits at C$34 to 100, which sets the price band.
30 people on the 6 pain cards this answers, 5% of the 631 people commenting on these 4 sub-steps. Read the comments
Sourcing and vendors
Ask Harnois for a snow rated walk-in greenhouse. Every greenhouse in the range is imported, and 41 people say kits buckle, rip or blow away. Harnois or BC Greenhouse Builders could quote an own brand kit for J1-T2.
51 people on the 7 pain cards this answers, 8% of the 600 people commenting on these 4 sub-steps. Read the comments
Sourcing and vendors
Ask a Québec heating maker for a heat mat quote. Heat mats rate medium for domestic supply, and certification is a barrier for importers. Rivals sell heat mat thermostats at about C$40, so quote a mat and thermostat set.
18 people on the 3 pain cards this answers, 2% of the 748 people commenting on these 3 sub-steps. Read the comments

In Journey 1, 65% of products are made in Canada or the US. The share is high because peat and seed products are Canadian. Every greenhouse in the range is imported.

Limits: this is a desk scan, with sources in the Method tab. A broker should check customs codes and any trade measures dated after mid 2026 before any business case.

Product typeDomestic whitespaceWhat the rating rests on
Frost cloth and row coverHighSpunbond fabric is made in North Bay, Ontario. Cutting and packing for retail needs little capital.
Cold frames and hoop kitsHighThese are long, awkward metal kits. Their inputs are domestic, and no Canadian retail brand is on the shelf.
Walk-in polycarbonate greenhousesHighThese are bulky to ship. Canada has aluminium and builders, such as BC Greenhouse Builders and Harnois.
Trays, inserts and domesMediumUS makers produce these at scale. Trays nest, which weakens the case for saving on freight.
Fibre and moulded-pulp potsMediumPeat pots are already made in Canada. Moulded pulp uses local recycled fibre.
Heat mats and thermostatsMediumCertification is a barrier for importers. A Québec heating maker exists.
Synthetic shrub coversMediumThese are imported today. They could use Ontario fabric, but sewing labour offsets the freight saving.
Peat pellets and mixesLow (already domestic)Peat is Canadian already. Coir comes from India and Sri Lanka.
LED grow lightsLowSupply is moving from China to Southeast Asia. North America isn't picking it up.
Mini greenhousesLowThese are low cost, compact kits with sewn covers that take a lot of labour.

Thin spots and limitsThree sub-steps rest on few comments. Most comments come from keen gardeners online.
  • These sub-steps have thin evidence: buy seedlings instead of starting (35 comments), transplant seedlings outdoors (18), replace failed plants (33), replace failed lights or trays (34) and grow food indoors through winter (34). We show them as they are and haven't padded them.
  • Keen hobbyists wrote most of what we read. Beginners and homeowners wrote less, so their rows on the map show only steps with 8 or more comments.
  • Canadian sources account for 43% of the journey's comments. They include Canadian subreddits, canadiantire.ca reviews and comments that name a Canadian place. The rest are benchmark comments, mostly from the US, or of unknown origin.
  • We kept canadiantire.ca reviews copied from brand sites (19%) and incentivized reviews, and gave them lower weight.
3
Opportunities
This section starts with the fineline opportunities, which are gaps, fixes, say it better and speak louder. Territories, roadmap moves and new product areas follow.
Fineline gaps: source or create (37)These are needs that no fineline serves, or that customers can't find. Each one points to bringing a product in, turnkeying one under own brand or developing a new one.
Sub-stepFinelineThe insightThe movePeople
Work out timing and frost datesNo finelineGrowers need local start and frost dates for each crop. Nothing in the range gives them, so seedlings start too early or too late, or die.Print zone-based dates for indoor starts, winter sowing and fall planting on seed racks and online.41
Choose a greenhouse or cold frameGreenhousesSerious growers want more space and strength for the money. Kits feel small, overpriced or sold out to them, so many build their own.Develop a 2x4 greenhouse bracket kit with polycarbonate panels, and stock kits deeper in season.29
Manage greenhouse heat and ventingNo finelineGrowers need heat that holds overnight. Barrels and buried pipe add little. Heaters fall short, and electric heat costs a lot.Bring in a thermostat-controlled greenhouse heater with a bubble insulation liner sized for kit greenhouses.26
Assemble and anchor the greenhouse or cold frameGreenhousesMany growers skip kits and build cold frames, hoop houses and benches from salvage. Lower-cost formats are the opening.Bring in a cold frame kit, a hoop house kit and greenhouse benches at entry prices.24
Choose frost and winter coversNo finelineShoppers want covers in the right size and weight at a fair price. Today the covers sell online, outside the range, in thin burlap and few sizes.Range frost covers in store, with heavier burlap, larger sizes, poly options and value rolls.21
Watch weather and windNo finelineMiracleGro and NuVue covers come without pegs or anchors, so covers and whole greenhouses blow away. Anchor kits sit in other departments.Bring the CANOPIA anchoring kit and ShelterLogic auger anchors into the garden range beside greenhouses and covers.21
Prepare covers and supportsNo finelineCovers need holding down in wind. NuVue stakes snap and tab ties fail. Quest covers come without ties.Bring in steel ground staples and cover clips, and pack strong stakes and ties with covers.20
Plan greenhouse heatingNo finelineGrowers need affordable greenhouse heat in the right size. Heaters sold elsewhere aren't made for damp greenhouses, and stoves or buried pipe cost too much.Bring in a damp-rated greenhouse heater with thermostat, sold with a sizing chart by floor area.19
Check germination and seedling healthNo finelineGrowers follow packet directions and still get poor, uneven sprouting, which points to bad batches. No seed fineline serves this step.Bring in germination tested seed with the test date printed, backed by a resow replacement.19
Grow seedlings under lightsNo finelineGrowers need trays that hold full, wet flats, and they need guidance on bottom watering. Jiffy trays bend and spill.Bring in a rigid, solid-bottom tray with a printed bottom watering guide.18
Watch seedlings for problemsNo finelineGrowers can't read the warning signs. They don't know when to vent domes, why leaves yellow or why seedlings stall at their first true leaves.Create a seedling trouble card for seed starting displays and online: dome venting, yellow leaves, stalled growth.15

Opportunity territoriesThe journey splits into 7 territories. Each one is a different outcome the customer wants, so no sub-step sits in two. Open a territory to see what customers struggle with, what Canadian Tire sells today and the moves for each team.
J1-T1Sow seeds that sprout in gear that holds upCanadian Tire wins on price for the 72 pellet kit. The opening is in trays and domes that crack and leak, refills that cost more than elsewhere, and an own brand tray listed as Jiffy.1,045 comments - 32% complaints35 pain points - 5 hacks7 sub-steps

Thin trays are the most counted pain in the journey. Trays that bend when wet, domes that crack and trays that leak follow close behind. Growers rebuy these parts each spring, and Canadian Tire charges more for them. Own brand has one tray and one dome, at one tier. A heavy, reusable own brand tray system, sold as a kit and as parts, would answer the complaint and the refill price together.

A returning grower who reuses last year's kit and finds 72 count refills hard to get and priced close to a new kit.

People, and their share of everyone commenting on that sub-step. Click a line to read the comments.
  • Product fails14 (4% of 325) - Seed trays are thin and flimsy, cracking when separated and buckling when carried full of soil. comments →
  • Product fails12 (4% of 325) - Propagation domes are thin and flimsy, and crack, crimp or deform when handled or stacked. comments →
  • Product fails11 (3% of 325) - Trays shown as solid arrive with holes, so they leak and can't be used for bottom watering. comments →
  • Price11 (3% of 325) - Seed trays and starter kits feel overpriced, and some buyers would only buy them on sale. comments →

Price against the market
  • On the same kit, Canadian Tire wins. The McKenzie/Jiffy 72 pellet kit is C$18.99, against C$19.48 at Home Depot and C$19.49 at Walmart.
  • Refills cost more. A dome is C$2.99 against C$2.48 at Home Depot. A 72 cell insert is C$8.99 against C$7.48 at Home Depot and C$8.47 at Walmart.
  • Jiffy seed starting mix, 13.2 L, is C$9.99 against C$7.45 at Home Depot. Canadian Tire sells pellets only in 36 packs, while others sell 72 and 200.
What Canadian Tire sells today
  • Seed Starting: 16 products, 2 own brand (Garden Club) and 14 competitive, C$2.99 to C$44.99, rated 4.29 on 904 ratings.
    This fineline rates well on the strength of McKenzie pellet kits. Own brand has one tray and one dome, both in the better tier.
  • Seed Starting Mixes: 5 products, no own brand, C$9.99 to C$14.99, rated 4.35 on 247 ratings.
    This fineline rates well, though growers report fast drying, coarse texture and gnats. The good and best tiers share one median price.
  • Grow Pots: 23 products, no own brand (Planters' Pride), C$0.49 to C$9.99, no ratings.
    Pots are there for potting up. Small tray cells force growers to pot up early, and sleeves don't break down.
  • Indoor Watering: 5 products, no own brand, C$9.99 to C$26.99, no ratings.
    Watering tools sit away from seed starting, even though overwatering and mould kill seedlings.
Moves by team
Sourcing and vendors
  • Respec trays and domes with thicker plastic, truly solid bottoms and rims that snap onto the tray. This fixes the most counted pain in the journey. It also fixes holes in trays sold as solid and domes that let humidity out.
  • Stock 72 and 200 pellet refills and tall domes for standard trays, priced below kits. Refills are hard to find and cost close to a kit. Competitors sell 72 and 200 counts.
  • Audit pellet counts and have McKenzie test kit seed pods by lot. Buyers report short counts, broken pellets and many duds from McKenzie pellet kits.
Product, design and engineering
  • Heavy, reusable own brand trays with deeper cells and vented domes, sold as kits and parts. Own brand has no good or best tier here. Deeper cells delay potting up, and selling parts keeps refills competitive.
  • Pellet mesh and pot sleeves that break down in soil, tested in beds. Mesh that stays intact restricts roots and litters beds.
Brand and marketing
  • Sell the Garden Club tray and dome under the Garden Club name. Shoppers don't see the own brand today, because both items are listed on canadiantire.ca as Jiffy.
  • Print sowing steps, dome venting and heat mat timing in the lid, with QR video. Beginners can't tell how to sow pellets, or when to lift the dome and leave the mat.
  • Make the McKenzie 72 cell pellet greenhouse the hero kit, with its star rating on shelf. It holds 4.28 from 236 ratings and already beats Home Depot and Walmart on price.
Who does it best today. Professional tray makers such as East Jordan Plastics mould propagation trays from recycled resin in the US, and heavy duty trays sell elsewhere at C$12.50.
The catch. A heavier own brand tray costs more to make. The kit's price lead over Home Depot and Walmart is thin.
Test first. Ask returning growers whether they would pay more for a tray and dome that last years, or keep buying cheap ones each spring.

J1-T2Greenhouses and cold frames that go up and stay standingCanadian Tire beats Home Depot on price for the Palram Hybrid 6 x 8. Anchors sit in another department, spare covers aren't sold, and growers build cold frames from salvage.823 comments - 35% complaints26 pain points - 7 hacks4 sub-steps

Wind is the thread through this territory. Kits buckle, mini greenhouses tip, whole greenhouses lift off their base, and covers split at the zipper within months. Most fixes are parts Canadian Tire can range now, such as anchors, spare covers and panel clips, plus a cold frame and a sturdier mid price kit. Walk ins are bulky to ship, which favours a Canadian built, snow rated kit.

A grower whose mini greenhouse tipped over in wind and spilled the seedlings, and whose zippered cover split within a month or two.

What Canadian Tire sells today
  • Greenhouses: 16 products, no own brand, C$59.99 to C$3,699.99, rated 4.01 on 246 ratings. Walk ins from C$679.99 rate 3.63 on 124..
    Walk ins rate lowest, and that is where assembly time, missing parts and wind failures pile up.
  • Other department: CANOPIA anchoring kit for sheds and shelters, and ShelterLogic 30 in auger anchor kit for shelters, both sold outside Seasonal and Gardening.
    Canadian Tire already sells answers to blow overs, and the opening is to place them beside the greenhouses that blow over.
Moves by team
Sourcing and vendors
  • Bring the CANOPIA anchoring kit and ShelterLogic auger anchors beside greenhouses and covers. Covers come without anchors, so owners tie greenhouses to fences or weigh them with rock filled totes.
  • Spare covers, ribs and panels for every kit sold, with reinforced zippers and UV stable covers. Covers split at zippers within months, and one broken part means buying a whole new kit.
  • Bring in a cold frame and a Canadian built, snow rated walk in greenhouse. Growers build cold frames from salvage. Our Q3 sourcing review rates walk ins and cold frames high for domestic supply.
Product, design and engineering
  • Mini greenhouse with ground stakes, a tip strap and shelf clips in the box. Mini greenhouses tip over even when loaded, and wire shelves wobble unless zip tied.
  • Walk in kits with numbered parts, written steps and a base kit included. Picture only instructions and unlabelled parts stall assembly. Wooden bases warp without a pad.
Brand and marketing
  • Show the anchoring kit on greenhouse boxes and pages, with a plain anchoring guide. Owners don't know how to anchor a greenhouse on grass or soil against strong wind.
  • Shelf and online chart comparing glass, single and twin wall polycarbonate on heat and snow. Buyers get conflicting advice and can't tell which glazing suits them.
Who does it best today. BC Greenhouse Builders, family owned since 1951, rates its hobby kits for snow loads to 32 psf. Buyers doubt that online kits have that kind of stated strength.
The catch. Snow rated, Canadian built kits cost more. We have not confirmed the tariff code behind the 25% surtax advantage on imports.
Test first. Ask Palram and ShelterLogic for tested wind and snow ratings, and spare cover prices, for the kits Canadian Tire sells.

J1-T3Light and heat that grow sturdy seedlings indoorsCanadian Tire's best reviewed grow light is its own NOMA T5 strip, at 4.6 on 96, and it sells outside the seed starting range. The one heat mat sits at the top tier and has no thermostat.1,000 comments - 28% complaints41 pain points - 8 hacks7 sub-steps

Leggy seedlings trace back to weak, narrow or purple lights, fixed height stands and mats that run too hot. Growers build racks from spare shelving and set the height with zip ties, because stands don't adjust or fit home shelves. NOMA already earns the strongest own brand reviews. An own brand light, stand and thermostat mat set built around NOMA would turn those reviews into a station shoppers buy together.

A grower whose seedlings stretch under a single grow bulb, propping trays on books because the light stand won't adjust.

Price against the market
  • The Jiffy Hydro heat mat is C$44.99 at Canadian Tire against C$37.97 at Walmart. The light and stand is C$69.99 against C$59.97.
  • Generic mats sell for C$17 to 24 at Walmart and Lee Valley. Mat and thermostat bundles are common online.
What Canadian Tire sells today
  • Hydroponics: 17 products, no own brand, C$12.99 to C$149.99, rated 4.22 on 118 ratings.
    Most are Hydrofarm brands. The Jiffy Grow Light leads at 4.41, and the Jump Start T5 system trails at 3.78.
  • Site only: 4 own brand NOMA grow lights, rated 4.1 to 4.6. The T5 strip is C$39.99, rated 4.6 on 96..
    Own brand's strongest products sell in another department, outside Seasonal and Gardening. Strip buyers can't get linking cables.
  • Seed Starting: 9 products, 2 own brand (Garden Club), C$2.99 to C$69.99, rated 4.21 on 566 ratings.
    The station tops out at C$69.99. The one heat mat sits in the best tier at C$44.99.
Moves by team
Sourcing and vendors
  • Range NOMA T5 strips and grow bulbs in the seed starting bay and online. These lights are own brand, rated 4.4 to 4.6, and Canadian Tire already sells them in another department.
  • Stock linking cables in short and long lengths, and spare tubes, beside each light. Linking cables are missing or too short. A burnt out bulb means replacing the whole fixture.
  • Require burn in testing and longer warranties from grow light and heat mat vendors. Lights and mats die within hours to months, with NOMA named most often.
Product, design and engineering
  • Own brand heat mat with thermostat at an opening price. Mats without thermostats cook seeds. Generic mats sell for C$17 to 24 elsewhere.
  • Height adjustable stand with ratchet hangers and brackets that fit home shelving. Stands are flimsy and fixed height, and brackets don't fit shelves. Growers make do with zip ties and books.
Brand and marketing
  • Label each light for seedlings, greens or fruiting, with true watts, PAR and certification. Shoppers can't compare lights, distrust inflated wattage and fear uncertified no name lights.
  • Print hours on, hanging height and heat mat timing by growth stage on each box. Conflicting advice on hours and height burns plants. Mats left on after sprouting cause legginess.
  • Label NOMA bulbs for single plants and point tray growers to the NOMA T5 strip. Buyers expect one bulb to light a tray, but it suits one or two plants.
Who does it best today. At Canadian Tire, the NOMA T5 strip at 4.6 on 96 and the Jiffy Grow Light at 4.41 earn the best reviews. Lee Valley sells cULus certified seedling mats.
The catch. Lights and mats are value dense electronics with Asian supply chains. The edge comes from spec, certification and fit, not from where they are made.
Test first. Ask the NOMA vendor whether the T5 strip can ship with linking cables and a hanging kit, and at what cost.

J1-T4Greenhouses that stay warm at night and cool by dayGreenhouse owners swing between frying seedlings by day and losing all their heat by night. Canadian Tire sells its heaters in other departments, and none is made for a damp greenhouse.513 comments - 26% complaints15 pain points - 2 hacks3 sub-steps

Overheating and night heat loss are the two largest greenhouse pains in the journey. Owners improvise with bubble wrap, water barrels and aquarium heaters. The range doesn't yet include a damp rated heater or greenhouse insulation. A climate offer sized to the greenhouse, with heat, insulation, a vent opener and a min max sensor, would answer both ends of the day.

An owner whose greenhouse fries seedlings on a sunny afternoon, then drops to near the outside temperature that night.
What customers struggle with
People, and their share of everyone commenting on that sub-step. Click a line to read the comments.
  • Product fails14 (8% of 185) - Greenhouses and plastic tents overheat in sun, reaching temperatures that fry seedlings. comments →
  • Product fails13 (7% of 185) - Greenhouses drop to outside temperature or colder at night, even after hot days. comments →
  • Knowledge gap8 (4% of 185) - Water barrel thermal mass adds little heat, so owners who try it still need a heater. comments →

  • Knowledge gap5 (5% of 107) - Water barrels are often suggested as heat stores, but owners find they make little difference in cloudy winters. comments →
  • Hack3 - Lines walls and doors with bubble wrap, foam board or shower curtains instead of buying insulated panels
What Canadian Tire sells today
  • Greenhouses: 2 products, no own brand (CANOPIA by PALRAM), good tier, C$99.99 to C$129.99, no ratings.
    Little in this fineline manages climate. Growers say kit vents are too small and openers break.
  • Other department: NOMA baseboard convector and Mastercraft ceramic barrel heater, 1500 W with thermostat, sold in heating.
    Thermostat heat is sold, but neither heater is made for a damp greenhouse.
  • Other department: Accutemp indoor/outdoor thermometer with humidity meter, sold in hardware.
    Owners need to see heat and humidity swings. The meter sits outside the garden range.
Moves by team
Sourcing and vendors
  • Bring in a damp rated greenhouse heater with thermostat, tip over shutoff and sizing chart. Owners can't size a heater and find current ones unsafe. Heaters sold elsewhere aren't made for damp greenhouses.
  • Bring in greenhouse bubble insulation with frame clips, cut to common kit sizes. Owners line walls with bubble wrap and foam board that falls off and leaves gaps.
  • Automatic vent openers with manual override, plus fitted shade cloth for kit greenhouses. Openers break or open on freezing sunny days. Owners open covers by hand daily.
Product, design and engineering
  • Larger roof vents and roll up doors on kit greenhouses, bundled with the Accutemp meter. Kit vents are too small to cool in summer. Trapped humidity brings mould and damping off.
Brand and marketing
  • Heater sizing chart by greenhouse floor area, at shelf and online. Owners feel overwhelmed choosing and sizing a heater for their greenhouse and climate.
  • Say plainly what water barrels, insulation and soil heating add in cloudy winters. Owners put effort into barrels and buried pipe that add little heat.
The catch. Heating a greenhouse costs a lot each month, and some growers say winter produce costs more than it is worth.
Test first. Ask the NOMA and Mastercraft heater vendors whether a damp rated version with tip over shutoff exists or can be certified.
Sub-steps: Plan greenhouse heating, Heat and insulate the greenhouse, Manage greenhouse heat and venting
J1-T5Plant out early and harvest late under coverGrowers build their own low tunnels and bend conduit on homemade jigs, because the range has no frost cloth, row cover, cloche or hoop kit. Lee Valley carries the full line.475 comments - 18% complaints14 pain points - 3 hacks6 sub-steps

Growers' hacks point to the brief. They build tunnels from PVC and conduit, upturn buckets over plants and drape bedsheets on stakes. None of it is big ticket, and other retailers sell frost cloth from C$10.99 and hoop kits from C$34.09. A hoop and frost cloth kit sized to Canadian Tire raised beds, with stakes that hold, would give own brand a home in season extension.

A grower who hauls potted plants indoors on every frost night and upturns buckets over the beds.

Sourcing and vendors
  • Bring in a low tunnel kit with pre bent steel hoops, fitted frost fabric and clips. Growers build tunnels from PVC and conduit and bend hoops on homemade jigs.
  • Steel ground staples and cover clips, packed with covers and sold loose. Plastic stakes snap during install, and cover edges lift in wind.
  • Frost cloth and row cover converted in Canada from Ontario spunbond. Our Q3 sourcing review rates frost cloth converting high. Spunbond is made in North Bay, Ontario, and converting needs little capital.
Product, design and engineering

  • Wheeled seedling shelf with a zip cover that rolls out mornings and back at night. Hardening off means carrying trays in and out daily, which is hard to fit around work.
Brand and marketing
  • Print a hardening off routine on the mini greenhouse box: shade, covered nights, full sun. Growers don't know how much sun, shade or night cold seedlings can take.
  • Frost cloth packs that state leaf contact, wet plants and how long to leave it on. Growers don't know how long covers can stay on or how to use frost cloth.
Who does it best today. Lee Valley carries the full season extension line of frost cloth, cold frames, hoop kits and a heat mat thermostat. Canadian Tire has an opening in each.

J1-T6Know when to start, plant out and coverTiming is the most discussed planning question and the least served. Seed packets give no local start dates, and Canadian Tire's thermometer and soil meter sit away from the seeds.402 comments - 23% complaints12 pain points - 0 hacks4 sub-steps

Growers start seeds too early or too late, and they can't tell which crops to start indoors. Freak late frosts catch them out. They need information where they buy, with zone based start dates on packets and racks and a thermometer and soil meter beside the seeds. Canadian Tire has no own brand in seeds yet, and better packs cost more than best ones.

A grower who sets warm crops out early, then loses them to a freak late frost, and holds the rest indoors into June.

  • Seeds and Seed Kits: 23 products, no own brand, C$10.49 to C$14.99, no ratings.

Moves by team
Sourcing and vendors
  • Shelve the Panacea soil meter and Accutemp thermometer beside seeds, with a cold tolerance chart. Growers don't know what night temperatures seedlings can handle. Both tools sit in other departments.
  • Bring in early maturing pepper and tomato varieties under a short season sign. Bell peppers and big tomatoes don't ripen red before a short season ends.
  • Pilot regional vegetable transplants timed to local frost dates, from nearby growers. Shoppers find store bought transplants pricey or root bound. This range doesn't carry any today.
Product, design and engineering
  • An own brand soil and air thermometer with a frost alert. Late and surprise frosts kill tender plants set out early. That makes timing stressful for growers.
Brand and marketing
  • Print zone based indoor start, winter sowing and fall planting dates on racks and online. Packets give no local start dates. The zone guidance growers find is conflicting or outdated.
  • Mark each packet front with start indoors or sow direct, plus weeks before last frost. Growers can't tell which crops to start indoors and which to sow direct, or when.
The catch. National packs can't fit every zone. Wrong dates would repeat the outdated guidance growers already distrust.
Test first. Ask McKenzie whether zone based start and plant out dates can print on racks and packets for next season.

That would turn a well reviewed online range into a shelf Canadian Tire owns.

Moves by team
Sourcing and vendors
  • Source precut burlap wraps with a tighter weave, sized for common shrubs. Quest burlap has a loose weave, needs doubling and is awkward to cut.
  • Stock covers in store in larger sizes, heavier fabric and plastic free options. Covers come in odd shapes with no larger size. Stores also carry few options.
Product, design and engineering
  • Launch an own brand winter cover line in Canadian shrub and cedar sizes, with stated dimensions. The category is well reviewed and has no own brand yet. The Q3 notes say synthetic covers can use Ontario spunbond.
  • Add insulated frost blankets that layer inside tunnels and mini greenhouses for hard cold. Unheated tunnels and mini greenhouses add only a few degrees. Plants need more protection than that in hard cold.
Brand and marketing
  • Print frost protection level and fabric weight on the front of NuVue and Quest covers. Shoppers can't tell which fabric or weight protects their plants. The packaging doesn't explain it.
  • Add a wrapping and overwintering guide for cedars, roses, young trees and pots. Cedars brown and roses die back even when wrapped. Growers also don't know where to keep pots over winter.
Who does it best today. NuVue's reusable shrub cover is rated 4.6 on 231 ratings on canadiantire.ca. Buyers of reusable covers say they last several winters.
The catch. At least one NuVue cover is made in China. The range is well liked, so an own brand line has to beat a cover buyers already trust.
Test first. Ask NuVue whether it can supply larger, clearly dimensioned covers and a tighter burlap for the store range.

Journey 2 - Lighthouse 2

Clear snow, ice, leaves and storm debris from my property

Executive summary

Canadian Tire has product at nearly every step of snow, leaf and storm clean-up, and the openings come after the sale, in mid-storm jams and in the plow ridges and salt damage that no product fixes.

WHERE IT HURTS
Breakdowns draw the most complaints, along with the damage that plows and salt leave behind.
Fixing the gear draws a 61% complaint share across 1,343 comments. That is the highest share of any large step in the journey. Repairing the damage draws 78%. Choosing snow gear draws the most comments, with fewer complaints at 30%. Complaints means the share of comments that are negative, with mixed comments counted as half.
WHAT THE SHELF COVERS
Canadian Tire has product on the shelf at nearly every step, and the openings are in help and timing.
We matched no product to planning for winter, checking the gear before a storm, keeping up with repeat storms or hiring a crew. Certified parts are on the shelf, yet owners describe belts and pins missing when they need them mid-storm.
VALUE, BRANDS, SOURCING
Gas snowblowers and own-brand shovels win on price, and EGO and branded consumables have room to catch up.
Some forum buyers wait for points events and price matching. For them, the regular price is a reference point more than the price they pay. In powered tools, own brand reaches the better tier and stops there. Shovels and ice melt are the strongest domestic options.
1
The three questions
This section answers the three questions for this journey: value against other retailers, brand architecture and domestic manufacturing.
Q1 - Value against other retailersThe question“How does our value proposition compare to key competitors (brands and retailers)?”Canadian Tire is strongest on gas snowblowers and own-brand shovels. It has ground to make up against RONA on EGO, and on national-brand consumables. Some forum buyers pay the event price and treat the regular price as a reference.
What to do
Brand and marketing
Feature the YardForce 24 in as the snowblower value pick. The YardForce 24 in sells for C$699.99, which is C$199 below Walmart for the same machine. It also costs C$99 less than the RONA own brand 212cc at C$799.Rests on price gap vs Walmart, not on a count of people.
Buying
Reprice the EGO 765 CFM blower kit against RONA. The EGO blower kit is C$469.99 here and C$429 at RONA. RONA showed the EGO saw, snowblowers and shovel 7 to 12% lower on the day we checked.
5 people on the 1 pain card this answers, under 1% of the 681 people commenting on this sub-step. Read the comments
Sourcing and vendors
Ask vendors for battery sizes on Yardworks saws. At the better level, own brand pole saws sit 137% and chainsaws 82% above national medians. These medians cover different products, and battery size may explain part of the gap.Rests on price gap vs national medians, not on a count of people.
Buying
Add a value rock salt against RONA VALU+. RONA VALU+ sells 20 kg of rock salt for C$8.49, and Sifto sits at C$8.99 here. Alaskan Premium 9 kg is C$13.99 here and C$10.98 at Walmart.

Shares are of the comments we read, not of customers or sales. One person on two cards counts once.

Limits: we checked prices on 20 October 2026 on Home Depot, RONA, Walmart and Princess Auto pages. We compared them with Canadian Tire's regular prices in the Category Review. Amazon.ca blocked our reading and Costco showed no prices. Home Hardware prices did not load. Several competitor prices were temporary sales.

  • Gas snowblowers are the strongest value position. The YardForce 24 in sells for C$699.99, which is C$199 below Walmart's price for the same machine. The Champion 26 in, at C$1,199.99, sits 40% below the median for 26 to 30 in machines. Home Depot's PowerSmart 24 in (C$598) is the one machine priced below Canadian Tire's lowest. RONA's own-brand 24 in is C$799.
  • EGO matches RONA's regular price, and RONA discounts. The 16 in saw, the 24 and 28 in two-stage machines and the 12 in snow shovel carry the same regular price at both. On the day we checked, RONA showed them 7 to 12% lower. The EGO 765 CFM blower kit is C$469.99 at Canadian Tire and C$429 at RONA.
  • Own-brand 48V tools don't undercut rivals, except the snowblower. Yardworks sits above the median of similar kits by 15% on the blower, 24% on the pole saw and 13% on the 16 in saw. The Yardworks 48V 20 in snowblower kit sells for C$649.99, which is 35% below the median. The product list Canadian Tire shared doesn't give battery sizes for the other Yardworks kits, so battery size may explain part of the gap.
  • Same-brand consumables cost more at Canadian Tire. A 9 kg bag of Alaskan Premium is C$13.99 at Canadian Tire and C$10.98 at Walmart. A 20 kg bag of Sifto is C$8.99, against C$8.38 at Home Depot. Yardworks Ice Melter 20 kg works out to C$1.00/kg, the lowest price per kg of any premium melt we found.
  • For some forum buyers, the event price is the real price. In 27 comments, buyers time a purchase to Canadian Tire points events, such as 40x and 60x Triangle days that give about 16 to 24% back. In 73 comments, buyers talk about price matching. One buyer calls the regular price "slightly inflated". One reviewer praises how easy it is to get Certified parts at Canadian Tire.

Q2 - Brand architecture across good, better, bestThe question“Do we have the right brand architecture and assortment mix, and are our brands positioned appropriately across the Good-Better-Best spectrum?”Own brand holds the entry and middle of manual snow tools, and it is also the parts brand. In powered tools it reaches the better tier. Gas machines have no own brand.
What to do
Brand and marketing
Merge Mastercraft and Yardworks into one better level brand. Mastercraft and Yardworks share the better level in cordless snowblowers, leaf blowers, chainsaws and pole saws. One brand per level lets a shopper read the ladder at a glance.Rests on brand ladder overlap, not on a count of people.
Product development
Add Certified heavy duty parts at the middle level. Certified holds the good level in parts, 24 of 50, and belts, 32 of 42. 69 people say augers, chutes, belts and wheels break or loosen, which opens a tougher middle level.
67 people on the 9 pain cards this answers, 6% of the 1,040 people commenting on these 2 sub-steps. Read the comments
Buying
Rebalance range space toward choosing a snowblower. Choosing a snowblower holds 6% of products against 22% of people raising pains. Replacing worn parts holds 20% of products against 6% of people, so review which parts lines earn their space.Rests on range share vs pain share, not on a count of people.
Buying
Reprice gas chipper-shredders so best tops the ladder. In gas chipper-shredders, best has a C$1,114.99 median, below good at C$2,099.99 and better at C$2,899.99. Some tiers here are our estimate from price, so confirm them with the vendor.Rests on price ladder, not on a count of people.

Shares are of the comments we read, not of customers or sales. One person on two cards counts once.

Limits: the brand placement list Canadian Tire shared gives tiers by brand within each fineline. Where a brand holds several tiers, we split its products across them in price order and marked those tiers as estimates. They cover 33% of the products in this journey. A tier for each product would firm this up. We treat MAXIMUM as own brand.

  • Manual snow tools. Yardworks covers good, better and best in pushers, scoops and specialty tools. Garant, a national brand, sits at best only.
  • Parts. Certified is the good tier in snowblower belts (32 of 42), accessories (26 of 38) and parts (24 of 50). National parts brands (Laser, MTD, EGO, Greenworks) sit at better and best.
  • Powered tools stop at better. Yardworks and Mastercraft hold the better tier in cordless snowblowers, leaf blowers, chainsaws and pole saws. National brands hold all of best: EGO, Greenworks and Worx.
  • Own brand is absent from gas snowblowers (Briggs & Stratton, Toro), gas chainsaws (Husqvarna), gas chipper-shredders, and chains and bars (Oregon).
  • Ice melt. Yardworks covers good and better, and Alaskan sits at better. Yardworks PawProtect is sold on canadiantire.ca but isn't in the product list Canadian Tire shared.
  • Battery platforms decide the brand. The platform a buyer picks for the snowblower decides the blower and saw that follow. Owners also worry that a platform will be dropped.

Electric Chipper-ShreddersOwn brand wins hereOwn brand holds the fineline, and the pains are about leaves. 5 people say fall cleanup fills dozens of yard bags, and some shred leaves with a trimmer in a garbage can.Show leaf shredding on the Yardworks shredder box, signed 'fewer yard bags: shred leaves into bed mulch'.

Snow ScoopsOwn brand wins hereWe didn't find pains tied to scoops in the comments. The sourcing scan rates snow shovels, pushers and scoops high for domestic supply.Keep Yardworks across all three price levels, and hold its Canadian supply.

ScrapersA price level is missing10 people say plastic blades crack or wear down within a season, and 5 want replaceable wear strips. Those pains point to a tougher scraper at the top level.Add a Yardworks scraper at the top price level with a steel core handle and bolt on metal wear strips.
Snowblower AccessoriesA price level is missing25 people say chutes and augers clog in wet snow, and 12 say snow freezes in the auger. 40 people turn to cooking spray, hot water or block heaters instead.Add Certified accessories at the middle price level, starting with a cold rated anti stick chute spray and a fitted cover.
Snowblower BeltsA price level is missing6 people say auger and drive belts slip off or snap, some within days. Snowblower PartsA price level is missing69 people say augers, chutes, belts and wheels break or loosen, often in early uses. That points to a tougher own brand part at the middle level. 17 can't find parts for working machines.Add Certified heavy duty parts at the middle level: steel augers, metal chute controls and universal fit shear pin packs.
Chainsaw AccessoriesNational brands leadSharpening tools follow the chain brands. 7 people don't know how to grind chains, and 5 say saws come without bar oil, so new owners can't cut on day one.Shelve bar oil beside every saw, and post a chain to file size chart at the sharpening shelf.
Chainsaw Chains & BarsNational brands leadChains and bars must fit specific saws, so the brand carries the trust. 16 people want tensioners that hold, and 6 swap stock chains for Oregon or Stihl.Sign Oregon chains as the upgrade for stock chains, and stock metal tensioner kits for Yardworks and EGO saws.
Cordless ChainsawsNational brands leadBattery saws ride on platforms, and own brand would struggle to earn trust at the top. 24 people say packs last 30 to 45 minutes, and 15 say saws bog on thicker wood.Make the EGO 18 inch saw the storm cleanup hero, and bundle a second large battery with the top saws.
Cordless Leaf Blowers & VacuumsNational brands leadThe battery platform drives this choice. 26 people keep a gas blower for big jobs, 24 say packs run down before the job is done, and 13 say rivals refuse price matches.Hero the EGO 765 CFM blower, and source a cordless leaf vacuum on each battery platform carried.
Cordless PolesawsNational brands leadPole saws ride on battery platforms. 9 people say extended pole saws are heavy and tiring, and 5 say batteries run down in minutes or falter in the cold.Choose national pole saws with lighter shafts and larger batteries, and print a safe high cut guide on each pack.
Cordless SnowblowersNational brands leadBattery platforms decide the brand, and the sourcing scan rates cordless tools low for domestic supply. 49 people say spare batteries cost hundreds of dollars, and 45 say blowers bog in wet snow.Lead with the EGO self propelled two stage, bundle a second battery in kits, and publish one clear price match policy.
Gas ChainsawsNational brands leadGas saws are engine products, and own brand has no position here. 5 people say gas saws are hard to pull start, and 5 say rarely used saws need carb work.Pair each gas saw with ethanol free fuel and bar oil, and add an easy start model.
Gas Leaf Blowers & VacuumsNational brands leadGas blowers are engine products led by a trusted brand. 8 people say battery blowers clear only light snow, and 6 say gas blowers are loud.Feature the Husqvarna backpack as the big yard hero, and source a quieter gas model with its noise rating shown.
Gas SnowblowersNational brands leadGas machines rely on engines, dealers and parts, and own brand has no position here. 82 people want a durable, easy starting machine at a fair price, and 19 can't judge a deal.Bring in a compact two stage model with electric start and stocked parts, and post a driveway size selector at shelf.
Leaf Blower AccessoriesNational brands leadAccessories have to fit a blower platform. 7 people say blow tubes come in one length, and 3 say gutter kits get heavy overhead and fall short.Source extension and short blow tubes for core platforms, and list which blowers each gutter kit fits.

Q3 - Domestic manufacturing and sourcingThe question“Are there any whitespace opportunities or priority categories where domestic manufacturing is particularly strong and could present additional development potential?”Bulky, simple products make the strongest domestic options: shovels and pushers, ice melt and salt, and paper leaf bags. Production of powered tools and batteries is moving within Asia. North America isn't picking it up.
What to do
Sourcing and vendors
Sign a dedicated Canadian source for Yardworks snow tools. All 15 pushers and 9 scoops are made in Canada today. Garant, Canada's leading snow tool maker, has a parent group moving toward China, which opens room for a dedicated private-label source.Rests on supply security, not a counted pain, not on a count of people.
Product development
Spec a deep cold Yardworks melt blended near distribution centres. Canada and the US make all chloride inputs, and blending and bagging needs little capital. 5 people say melt stops working near minus 7, an opening for J2-T7.
5 people on the 1 pain card this answers, 3% of the 195 people commenting on these 2 sub-steps. Read the comments
Sourcing and vendors
Ask an Ontario converter for paper leaf bags. Paper leaf bags use domestic kraft paper, and the 50% counter-tariff on US paper favours converting in Canada. 5 people say fall cleanup fills dozens of yard bags, an opening for J2-T4.
5 people on the 1 pain card this answers, 1% of the 502 people commenting on these 2 sub-steps. Read the comments
Sourcing and vendors
Ask Wallenstein to quote an own brand chipper-shredder. Wallenstein already builds chipper-shredders in St. Clements, Ontario. Engines are imported, and we haven't verified where the current range is made, so the quote comes first.Rests on domestic maker, not on a count of people.

Shares are of the comments we read, not of customers or sales. One person on two cards counts once.

In Journey 2, 27% of products are made in Canada or the US. Most of the Canadian share is own-brand, manual product. That includes snow pushers (13 of 15 own brand, made in Canada), scoops (8 of 9), specialty snow tools (5 of 7) and ice melters (7 of 10). The US share is mostly Oregon chains and accessories.

Limits: this is a desk scan. A customs broker should check trade measures dated after mid 2026, and the customs codes, before any business case.

Product typeDomestic whitespaceWhat the rating rests on
Cordless outdoor power equipment and battery platformsLowCells, electronics and platforms are made in China. Chervon and Greenworks are moving this work to Vietnam. In North America, US assembly is limited to platform owners like STIHL.
Gas two-stage snowblowers, gas chainsawsMediumThe US has a real manufacturing base: Ariens in Brillion, Toro in Windom and STIHL in Virginia. Section 232 tariffs favour US chainsaws. Stanley Black & Decker is exiting some gas lines. Canada has no assembler, and engines are imported.
Chipper-shreddersMediumWallenstein, a Canadian fabricator in St. Clements, Ontario, already builds them. Volumes are low and the units are bulky. Engines are imported, and we haven't verified where Canadian Tire's current range is made.
Snow shovels, pushers, scoopsHighGarant makes more than 4M tools a year in Québec. Its parent, AMES, is shifting toward China. These tools are bulky and cheap, and the tooling costs little. Canadian counter-tariffs penalize US-made tools.
Ice melters and rock saltHighCanada and the US make rock salt and all chloride inputs, at Goderich, Windsor, Ludington and Slave Lake. Blending and bagging near distribution centres needs little capital. Freight costs are high against the value of the product.
Leaf rakes and leaf bagsHigh for bags, medium for rakesPaper leaf bags are bulky and cheap, and they're made from domestic kraft paper. Ontario already has a converter. Canada's 50% counter-tariff on US paper favours converting in Canada.
Replacement partsMediumChain and bar makers already run plants in Guelph and Virginia Beach. Job shops could make pins and augers. OEM part numbers and small volumes limit that opening.

The journey and where it hurtsComplaints cluster after the purchase. Owners describe jams, broken belts and dead batteries mid-storm, and the ridge of packed snow and salt damage that plows leave. Choosing gear draws 3,221 comments, more than any other step, and a lower share of them are complaints.

Thin spots and limitsA few planning and upkeep sub-steps rest on few comments. The value evidence leans on a deals forum.
  • These sub-steps have thin evidence: Plan fall and storm clean-up (23 comments), Check the gear and the forecast (39 comments) and Clean leaves out of gutters (35 comments). We show them as they are, without padding.
  • Of the journey comments, 63% are from Canada: Canadian subreddits, RedFlagDeals, canadiantire.ca reviews and comments that name a Canadian place. The rest are benchmark comments, mostly from the US, or of unknown origin.
  • RedFlagDeals, a deals forum, supplies 4,031 comments. It is the best Canadian source we found. It tilts the value evidence toward sale timing, points events and price matching, so read Q1 with that in mind.
  • We kept canadiantire.ca reviews copied from brand sites, and incentivized reviews, but gave them lower weight. Home Depot Canada reviews did not load, so they are not included.
  • The trade measures in the sourcing scan dated after mid 2026 come from desk research. A broker should check them before any business case.

Opportunity territoriesThe journey splits into 7 territories. Each one is a different outcome the customer wants, so no sub-step sits in two. Open a territory to see what customers struggle with, what Canadian Tire sells today and the moves for each team.
J2-T1The right snow machine for my driveway and my snowCanadian Tire has a deep, well rated snowblower range and an own brand kit that wins on price. Buyers can't judge runtime, battery life or power on the plow ridge, so doubt about the battery weighs on the choice.3,404 comments - 30% complaints86 pain points - 2 hacks4 sub-steps

Choosing a snowblower is the busiest part of the journey. Battery cost, runtime and power in deep snow lead the complaints. The Yardworks 48V 20 in kit already sits 35% below the median of similar kits. Gas snowblowers have no own brand yet and rate 3.15. Canadian Tire can sell the choice by driveway and snow type, with honest runtime and a second battery, so buyers leave confident.

A buyer with a long driveway and a plow ridge, weighing a battery blower against gas and against a snow service that arrives late.
What customers struggle with
People, and their share of everyone commenting on that sub-step. Click a line to read the comments.
  • Price49 (3% of 1752) - Spare and replacement batteries cost hundreds of dollars each, close to the price of a whole gas blower comments →
  • Product fails42 (2% of 1752) - Battery blowers seem too weak for deep snowfalls and northern winters, so buyers stay with gas comments →
  • Product fails37 (2% of 1752) - One charge doesn't clear a large driveway or several properties, so owners need many spare batteries comments →
  • Price25 (1% of 1752) - Battery blowers cost far more than gas machines of similar power comments →
  • Product fails17 (under 1% of 1752) - Battery blowers bog down in heavy wet snow and slush comments →
  • Hack3 - Pay a plow per visit, or only past a set depth, instead of buying bigger snow equipment
Price against the market
  • The Yardworks 48V 20 in snowblower kit is C$649.99, 35% below the C$998 median. RONA has Greenworks 20 in kits on sale at C$447 and C$629.99.
  • The EGO 56V 21 in kit is C$999.99 at Canadian Tire, right at the median. It comes with one 4Ah battery, and most rival kits come with two.
  • The YardForce 24 in two stage is C$699.99, which is C$199 below Walmart. Home Depot's PowerSmart 24 in is C$598, and RONA's own brand 24 in is C$799.
What Canadian Tire sells today
  • Cordless Snowblowers: 33 products: 5 own brand (Yardworks, Mastercraft) and 28 from other brands, C$249.99 to C$2,999.99, rated 4.41 on 2,868 ratings.
    Customers rate this range well. Own brand reaches up to the better tier. Doubt about the battery is what loses the sale.
  • Gas Snowblowers: 14 products, no own brand, C$699.99 to C$3,399.99, rated 3.15 on 115 ratings.
    This is Canadian Tire's strongest value position on price. It is also the lowest rated fineline here, and buyers staying with gas have no own brand to choose.
  • Electric Snowblowers: 2 products, both own brand (Certified), C$139.99 to C$199.99, rated 4.04 on 418 ratings.
    Buyers trust this entry price. They can't find a low priced electric blower with a metal auger. Cords also limit reach.
  • Snow Pushers: 15 products: 13 own brand (Yardworks) and 2 from Garant, C$24.99 to C$89.99, rated 4.46 on 1,458 ratings.
    Canadian Tire's own brand holds the manual snow tool shelf. The complaints sit with power shovels that clear only light snow.
Moves by team
Sourcing and vendors
  • Turnkey an own brand 24 in two stage gas snowblower with metal chute controls. Gas snowblowers have no own brand yet and rate 3.15. RONA already sells its own 24 in model at C$799.
  • Ship cordless snowblower kits with a second large battery and a steel auger. Runtime and plastic augers lead the failures owners report. The EGO 21 in kit has one battery, and most rival kits have two.
  • Bring in a dual power snowblower that runs on battery or a cord. Owners fear dead packs, discontinued platforms and storm outages. None of the cordless blowers in this range offers a plug in backup.
Product, design and engineering
  • Make an own brand wheeled power shovel with an adjustable chute and a stated snow depth. Power shovels clear only light snow and throw it straight ahead. Seniors find them too heavy to carry.
  • Offer a Certified corded snowblower with a steel auger at the entry price. Shoppers can't find a low priced electric blower with a metal auger. Plastic augers break on ice.
Brand and marketing
  • Label each cordless snowblower with area cleared per charge, snow depth handled and battery fit. Shoppers can't judge runtime, battery life, battery fit or plow ridge ability before buying.

  • Feature the EGO self propelled two stage in store as the gas replacement. Gas fumes, noise and oil changes push buyers toward electric. Cordless snowblowers rate 4.41.

Clearing is the second busiest step in the journey. The plow bank comes up in three steps. It stalls light blowers, takes hours to chip by hand and comes back after every storm. Owners chop it with a spade and take partial passes. Canadian Tire can source or make the answers to the biggest clearing complaints: a steel tool for the bank, tougher own brand pushers and a second battery.

  • A pet safe Yardworks melt that works as well as the regular melter. PawProtect rates 3.4 on 19 ratings, while the regular melter rates 4.43. Blended melt also rates high for domestic supply.
Brand and marketing
  • Show the price per kg on ice melt tags and online, starting with Yardworks 20 kg. Canadian Tire's own brand leads on price per kg. National brand bags cost more at Canadian Tire than at competitors.
  • Shelve the EasyHeat cable kit beside ice tools, with signs showing it stops overnight refreeze. Owners don't expect meltwater to refreeze at walks, garage doors and drains.
  • Feature the Yardworks melter and its 4.43 rating on the storm end cap. Across 1,611 ratings, customers already rate the own brand bag well on results.
Who does it best today. RONA carries calcium chloride flake, boxed CMA pet safe melt and EasyHeat roof and gutter cable kits. Shoppers find deep cold, pets and refreeze covered in one place.
The catch. A deep cold blend and steady storm week prices squeeze margin on a product customers buy mostly on price.
Test first. Test Yardworks, Alaskan and calcium chloride side by side on the same icy step below minus seven. Ask dog owners which one they trust.
Sub-steps: Get the driveway ready for snow, Choose ice melt, salt or traction aids, Melt ice and add traction, Watch for ice build-up and refreeze

Journey 3 - Lighthouse 1

Keep my pool clean, balanced, safe and ready

Executive summary

Aquarius chemicals and kits earn the most reviews in the pool journey, mostly positive, and the openings are in leaking liners, failing pumps and covers, and water tests people don't trust.

WHERE IT HURTS
Leaks, failed gear and testing draw the most complaints.
Comments about fixing the pool and the gear run 71% complaints, across 703 comments. Watching the water and the gear runs 65%, and testing the water runs 49%. Complaints means the share of comments that are negative, with mixed comments counted as half.
WHAT THE SHELF COVERS
The range covers chemicals and accessories. Testing, repair and covers have few products so far.
The range has openings for a drop kit that reads free chlorine, alkalinity or stabilizer, and for a suction-side cleaner. It has one sand filter pump, sold online only, and two repair products. Most chlorine and shock products are on canadiantire.ca but not in the Category Review.
VALUE, BRANDS, SOURCING
Kits and accessories hold their own on price. Branded gear costs more at Canadian Tire than at the specialists.
We can't price the core chlorine and shock against rivals yet. Aquarius products draw the most reviews, and most are positive. Own brand has one pool, and it has the lowest rating of any product in the journey's reviews. Balancers and hard-sided hot tubs are the strongest options for domestic supply.

The three questions
This section answers the three questions for this journey: value against other retailers, brand architecture and domestic manufacturing.

The core chemicals can't be compared yet.

These checks have limits. We checked prices on 20 October 2026 on Pool Supplies Canada, Pioneer, Walmart.ca, Home Depot and Costco pages. We compared them with Canadian Tire's regular prices in the Category Review. Home Depot and Costco showed no prices. The canadiantire.ca pages didn't load, so Canadian Tire prices come only from the Category Review.

  • Branded equipment costs more than at the specialists. The Aiper Scuba N1 is C$849.99 at Canadian Tire and C$599.97 at Pool Supplies Canada. The Steel Pro Max 15 ft pool is C$749.99 at Canadian Tire, against C$649. Some rival prices were sales. Even so, Pool Supplies Canada's regular N1 price of C$823.99 is still below Canadian Tire's.
  • We can't compare the core chemical basket. The product list Canadian Tire shared doesn't include trichlor pucks, shock, pool-size pH and alkalinity products, or algaecide. The canadiantire.ca site does list Aquarius and HTH pucks. Pool specialists charge C$8.33 to 12.50/kg for trichlor, C$15.53 to 17.60/kg for shock and C$5 to 7/kg for pH.
  • Spa sizes cost 2 to 3 times more per kg. Canadian Tire sells pH Plus at C$19.98/kg, while specialists sell a 2 kg pool size at C$7.00/kg. Hot tub bromine sits mid-market at C$37.99/kg.
  • Kits and accessories hold their ground. Aquarius opening and closing kits cost C$32.99 to 46.99, below rival kits at C$47.95 to 64.99. We haven't compared what's inside them. The Kokido Telsa 5 handheld vac costs C$99.99, the lowest price we found.
  • Walmart.ca is a marketplace, not a single low price. Its third-party sellers mark up specialist chemicals by 30 to 167%. Walmart.ca puts its real pressure on equipment. An Intex solar cover sells for C$54.98 against C$99.99, and inflatable spas start at C$469.99 against C$899.99.
  • Reviewers back the chemical prices. Canadian reviewers on canadiantire.ca say Canadian Tire's chemicals are fairly priced against local pool companies. They buy them on sale or on points days. Forum posters see Canadian Tire's low-cost solar blankets as one-season products.

We set the tier by price within a brand for 56% of the products in this journey, so those tiers are our estimate. Treat the tier pattern as a guide until Canadian Tire confirms the tier for each product. Aiper has no brand listed in the product list Canadian Tire shared. We count it as a national brand.

  • Aquarius covers good, better and best in pool water treatment, with 25 of 40 products. All 17 own-brand spa chemicals sit in the better tier. Aquarius also covers opening and closing kits and winterizing gear.
  • One own-brand pool. The Outbound steel frame pool sits in the better tier. Reviewers give it 2.6 stars, the lowest in the journey's reviews, and mention seam leaks. Coleman, Intex, Hydro-Force and Bestway supply the rest of the pools.
  • No own brand yet. Pool covers come from Bestway, robotic cleaners from Aiper, spas from SaluSpa, Canadian Spa Company and Coleman, and spa filters from Excel.
  • Chlorine and shock are missing from the Category Review. Canadian Tire lists 21 Aquarius and HTH puck and shock products on canadiantire.ca. We need to place them before we can finish Q1 and Q2 for chemicals.

In Journey 3, 15% of products are made in Canada or the US. Most of these are own-brand chemicals, 20 of 27. They include spa chemicals made in Canada (10 of 17 own brand), 4 opening kits and 3 closing kits. The Canadian Spa Company hard-sided spa also counts. Pools, pumps, filters, covers and robots are imported, mainly from China.

Limits: this is a desk scan. A customs broker should check trade measures dated after mid 2026, and the customs codes, before any business case.

Product typeDomestic whitespaceWhat the rating rests on
Chlorine and sanitizersMedium for tableting and packing, low for activesUS capacity for actives shrank when Conyers closed. Canada has no producer. A PMRA-registered Canadian tableter is plausible, though actives stay imported. Class 5.1 dangerous goods rules apply.
Balancers and specialty chemicalsHighUS plants make bicarbonate, bisulfate and calcium chloride from domestic inputs. Blending needs little capital and mostly needs no registration. The product is heavy, which suits local packing.
Test strips and kitsLowHach (Elkhart), LaMotte and Taylor already make them in the US. The product is light, so freight gives a new Canadian plant no advantage.
Pumps and sand/cartridge filtersMediumNorth America already has a base, with Hayward in Nashville, Waterway in Oxnard and Carvin in Saint-Hyacinthe. Hayward is cutting China's share of its cost of goods from 10% to 3%. Entry-level combos stay in Asia. Efficiency and CSA rules favour incumbents.
Robotic and suction cleanersLowChinese brands lead this consumer electronics category and are now moving to Vietnam, as the Aiper ruling of June 2026 shows. Maytronics is consolidating in Israel.
Winter and solar coversMediumBoth countries have proven fabricators, including GLI in Youngstown, Latham in Kingston and Midwest Canvas. Covers are bulky. We haven't verified where the film and scrim come from.
Steel-frame and inflatable poolsLowBestway will make every category in Vietnam by March 2027. The product is labour-heavy PVC. The domestic opening is in the adjacent category of steel-wall pools, made by Trévi in Mirabel.
Hot tubs and spa partsHigh (hard-sided)Several Canadian makers build tubs, including Arctic Spas in Alberta, Hydropool in Ontario, and Coast and Beachcomber in BC. Tubs are costly to ship. Section 338 puts their US exports at risk and may free capacity for Canadian Tire.

Thin spots and limitsTwo sub-steps rest on few comments. The chemical counts are limited by what the product list Canadian Tire shared includes.
  • Set up the hot tub has 18 comments and Use pool chemicals for other jobs has 8, so both are thin. We show them as they are, without padding.
  • Of the comments in this journey, 53% come from Canada. That share comes from Canadian subreddits, RedFlagDeals, canadiantire.ca reviews and comments that name a Canadian place. The rest are benchmark comments, mostly from the US, or of unknown origin.
  • RedFlagDeals, a deals forum, supplies 1,325 comments. It is the best Canadian source we found. It also tilts the value evidence toward sale timing, points events and price matching, so read Q1 with that in mind.
  • We kept canadiantire.ca reviews copied from brand sites, and incentivized reviews, but gave them lower weight. Home Depot Canada reviews did not load, so they are not included.
  • The trade measures in the sourcing scan dated after mid 2026 come from desk research. A broker should check them before any business case.
  • Most pool chlorine and shock products are on canadiantire.ca but not in the Category Review. The range table counts them, though their tiers and origin are unknown.

Opportunity territoriesThe journey splits into 7 territories. Each one is a different outcome the customer wants, so no sub-step sits in two. Open a territory to see what customers struggle with, what Canadian Tire sells today and the moves for each team.
J3-T1Covers, heat and closing that stretch the seasonAquarius opening and closing kits rate well and cost less than rival kits. The covers and solar heaters around them are national brands that run small, rip and barely warm the water.1,238 comments - 35% complaints39 pain points - 9 hacks8 sub-steps

Owners raise complaints about covers and heaters when they choose, use and replace them. Bestway covers run small for the pool on the label and break down in the sun. GAME solar panels give little or no temperature rise. Closing the pool is mostly know how, from how low to drain the water to which chemicals go in and in what order. An own brand cover line and a closing system built around the Aquarius kit answer both ends of the season.

An above ground pool owner closing for the first time, unsure how far to lower the water or what to plug. In spring, they find cracked pump fittings.
What customers struggle with
People, and their share of everyone commenting on that sub-step. Click a line to read the comments.
  • Product fails24 (13% of 178) - Solar pool heaters give little or no temperature rise, even after days in full sun. comments →
  • Product fails16 (10% of 154) - Pool, solar and winter covers are thin, and many rip or get holes within days or a season comments →
  • Product fails15 (16% of 91) - Pool covers break down in the sun within a season, shedding bubbles and plastic bits into the pool. comments →
  • Product fails13 (8% of 154) - Pool covers run too small for the pool size on the label, some about 2 ft short comments →
  • Product fails9 (3% of 294) - Pumps, filters, skimmers and connectors crack over winter when water is left in them comments →
  • Hack4 - Builds a homemade solar heater from black tubing or pipe instead of buying kit solar panels.
Price against the market
  • Aquarius closing kits cost C$35.99 for above ground pools and C$46.99 for in ground pools. Both sit below competing kits at C$47.95 to C$64.99. We did not check what the Canadian Tire kits contain.
  • Canadian Tire sells the Blue Wave 18 ft mesh winter cover at C$94.99. Pool Supplies Canada and Pioneer sell solid 18 ft covers at C$49.99.
  • Canadian Tire's 18 ft solar cover is C$99.99, and Walmart sells an Intex 18 ft cover at C$54.98. Canadian Tire's 22 to 24 ft cover is C$124.99, below hard wall 24 ft covers at C$169.99 to C$179.99.
What Canadian Tire sells today
  • Pool Covers: 11 products, all Bestway with no own brand, priced C$21.99 to C$124.99 and rated 3.4 on 265 ratings.
    Pool cover complaints land on one national brand. That leaves room for an own brand cover cut true to size.
  • Pool Closing Kits: 3 products, all Aquarius, priced C$18.99 to C$46.99 and rated 4.66 on 126 ratings.
    This is a trusted own brand anchor for fall. Canadian Tire can build plugs, pillows, antifreeze and clear closing steps around it.
  • Pool Winterization Equipment: 7 products, 4 Aquarius and 3 Blue Wave or Bestway, priced C$5.99 to C$94.99, with no ratings.
    Plugs, pillows and winter covers are on the shelf. Owners say the plugs leak and the pillows deflate or pop.
  • Pool Water Treatment: 1 heater, a GAME solar model with no own brand option, priced C$269.99 and rated 2.83 on 107 ratings.
    The range holds one low rated solar heater. Affordable heat for cool spring and fall weather is still open.
Moves by team
Sourcing and vendors
  • Bring in a plug in heat pump for above ground pools, with its running cost on the box. Gas heaters and heat pumps cost thousands, and solar barely warms the water. So owners build their own heaters from pipe and hose.
  • Stock solid winter covers, cover pumps and winter cover supports for above ground pools. Canadian Tire carries a mesh winter cover. Rain sinks covers, and snow load damages walls and skimmers.
  • Shelve WinterProof antifreeze and Mastercraft utility pumps with the pool winter gear. Both are sold outside the product list Canadian Tire shared. Pumps, filters and connectors crack when water is left inside.
Product, design and engineering

Owners still clean their pools by hand. Handheld vacuums stir up debris and let fine silt through, and poles flex. Robots stall on liner wrinkles, slopes and stairs. Cartridge filters clog within hours or days, so owners want to move away from them. Two steps sit between a hand vacuum and a robot: a suction side cleaner and a standalone sand filter combo. Canadian Tire doesn't carry either one in store yet.

Improving the Outbound pool and selling the base, footings and patch kit with it turns the own brand pool into a full kit.
