The catch. Tubs are big ticket purchases that need a lot of service. Selling more of them without a service partner would repeat the club store complaints buyers already voice.
Test first. Ask hot tub shoppers whether one bundled price with cover, chemicals and a local service partner would move them from a dealer.
Sub-steps: Decide on a pool or hot tub, Choose a hot tub and spa supplies, Set up the hot tub, Maintain the hot tub
The product roadmap lists moves that free up development timeMost gaps close with products that already exist. Canadian Tire can bring in a brand, put its own brand on a vendor product, adjust what's on the shelf, or borrow from another department. That leaves development time for the few new products below.
TerritoryMoveItemWhy
J3-T1 Longer seasonTurnkey under own brandOwn-brand solar and winter covers cut true to size, with tie down clipsCanadian Tire has no own-brand cover on the shelf yet. Fit and tearing lead the complaints.
J3-T1 Longer seasonBring in a brandA plug in heat pump for above ground pools, with the running cost on the boxOwners want shoulder season heat at a fair price. They build homemade heaters instead.
J3-T1 Longer seasonBorrow from another departmentMastercraft utility pumps and WinterProof antifreeze shown with winter gearCanadian Tire sells both outside the product list it shared. Freezing and water on the cover are problems at closing.
J3-T2 Clean poolBring in a brandAbove ground sand filter and pump combos in the store rangeCartridge clogging is the top filter complaint. The one sand pump in the range is sold online only.
J3-T2 Clean poolTweak an existing productStronger suction, finer bags and metal poles on Aquarius vacuumsOwners complain most about handheld suction, bags and poles when cleaning.
J3-T2 Clean poolBorrow from another departmentMastercraft 1/2 HP pump kit offered as the upgrade for kit poolsKit pumps packed with above ground pools are undersized and let algae grow.
J3-T3 Clear waterTweak an existing productPool size Aquarius balancers in 2 to 8 kg packsSpa sizes cost two to three times more per kg than pool sizes elsewhere.
J3-T3 Clear waterTweak an existing productDose by pool size and a stabiliser warning on Aquarius chlorine labelsOwners get confused about dosing as they choose, balance, shock and fix green water.
J3-T3 Clear waterTurnkey under own brandAn Aquarius season supply kit by pool sizePool Supplies Canada sells season kits at C$439.99 to C$899.99. The product list Canadian Tire shared has none.
J3-T4 Gear that lastsBring in a brandKokido and Outbound cartridges, bags and small parts in storeOwners can't find them in Canada and pay more in shipping than the part costs.
J3-T4 Gear that lastsTweak an existing productBattery cleaner vendors required to ship charged batteries and test after storageBattery cleaners fail out of the box and after winter storage.
J3-T4 Gear that lastsBorrow from another departmentMastercraft 1/2 HP pump kit offered at the parts wall as the replacementBundled pumps wear out within a season. Canadian Tire sells this kit outside the product list it shared.
J3-T5 Sound poolTweak an existing productOutbound frame pool with reinforced seams, thicker floor and a leak warranty past first fillThe one own-brand pool rates 2.6, among the lowest in the journey.
J3-T5 Sound poolBring in a brandBase pads and wide leg footings sized to each frame poolOwners describe sinking legs and improvised bases when setup goes wrong.
J3-T5 Sound poolBorrow from another departmentFlex Seal Pool Patch & Repair Kit shelved beside pools and linersLeak repair is the top complaint. Canadian Tire sells the kit outside the product list it shared.
J3-T6 Trusted testingBring in a brandA liquid drop test kit for free chlorine, pH, alkalinity and stabilizerOwners who distrust strips move to drop kits. The product list Canadian Tire shared has none.
J3-T6 Trusted testingTweak an existing productAquarius strips reformulated to match the chart, with a high range pad and expiryStrip accuracy is the largest single pain in the journey.
J3-T6 Trusted testingTweak an existing productThe product to add printed beside each colour on the strip chartOwners get readings but don't know what to add.
J3-T7 Hot tubTurnkey under own brandEach spa bundled with a cover and Aquarius chemicals at one starting priceBuyers can't pin down the full cost of owning a tub.
J3-T7 Hot tubBring in a brandHard sided tubs from Canadian makersBuyers want winter use. Hard sided tubs rate high for domestic supply.
J3-T7 Hot tubTweak an existing productGood and best tiers added to Aquarius spa chemicalsAll 17 own-brand spa chemicals sit at one tier.
New product development areasWe found 1 area where nothing on the shelf does the job well. It rests on a repeated complaint, and existing manufacturing can build it.
TerritoryAreaWhy
J3-T6 Trusted testingA dose wheel by pool volume packed with Aquarius strips, turning each reading into an Aquarius product and amountOwners can't act on their readings. Advice differs from one store to the next. Printed card stock uses existing manufacturing.

03 - Value

Value against other retailers

The question“How does our value proposition compare to key competitors (brands and retailers)?”
Executive summary

Canadian Tire holds or wins on gas snowblowers, the walk-in greenhouse and starter kits, and trails on repeat purchases like refills, consumables and spa-size chemicals. Branded equipment often costs more at Canadian Tire than at specialists.

60
price pain points across the three journeys
raised by 531 people

regular prices in the Category Review against rival shelf prices
WHERE CT WINS
Big-ticket machines and starter kits.
Most gas snowblowers price at or below rivals. So do the Yardworks 48V snowblower kit, the Champion chipper, the 72-pellet seed kit, own-brand shovels and the Kokido handheld vac. Pool opening and closing kits price below rival kits, though we haven't yet compared their contents.
WHERE CT LOSES
What customers buy again.
Seed-starting refills and domes cost more than at rivals. So do Alaskan and Sifto bags, and branded robots and pools. The Category Review lists only spa-size balancers, which cost 2 to 3 times the per-kg price of pool sizes elsewhere.
HOW THEY BUY
Event prices and price matching.
Some forum buyers time big purchases to points events and price matching. Treat the regular price as a reference. These buyers pay the event price.
Where Canadian Tire wins and loses on priceIn all three journeys, Canadian Tire competes on starter kits and core machines. It trails rivals on many repeat purchases.

Our brands against competitor brandsInside Canadian Tire, own brand is priced below national brands in pool chemicals, pool parts and most manual tools, and above them in cordless tools.

This view compares own-brand and national-brand products in the same fineline and at the same price level, using regular prices from the product list Canadian Tire shared and canadiantire.ca ratings. It compares medians across different products, so a gap can come from kit contents or size as well as price.

  • Pool chemicals and parts. Aquarius sits well below the national brands at every level of pool water treatment, and customers rate the two about the same (3.97 against 3.99).
  • Cordless tools. Yardworks and Mastercraft sit above national brands at the middle level in cordless snowblowers, chainsaws and pole saws. In cordless snowblowers, customers rate the Mastercraft machine 3.73 on 86 ratings and the national brands 4.43 on 2,782, so the higher price buys less trust.
  • Electric blower vacs. Own brand costs less than the national brands at the same levels, and customers rate it higher (4.28 against 4.07). That makes it the clearest own-brand win on value.

Journey 1 - Start earlier, protect longer: value in detailOn identical items, Canadian Tire wins the first purchase and other retailers win the refills. Big-ticket items hold up on price. Season-extension gear is sold at other retailers, which makes it an opening here.

Limits: we checked prices on 20 October 2026, in the off-season, from Home Depot, Walmart and Lee Valley pages. Amazon.ca blocked automated reading, and RONA and Costco showed no prices, so the ranges leave them out. Several competitor items were out of stock.

  • Same kit, dearer refills. The McKenzie with Jiffy 72-pellet kit costs C$18.99 at Canadian Tire, C$19.48 at Home Depot and C$19.49 at Walmart. The parts a returning grower buys again cost more here. The dome is C$2.99 against C$2.48, and the Pro-Hex tray is C$8.99 against C$7.48 to 8.47. The 36-pellet refill is C$6.49 against C$5.98, and 13.2 L of Jiffy mix is C$9.99 against C$7.45.
  • Jiffy Hydro costs 17 to 19% more than at Walmart. The heat mat is C$44.99 against C$37.97, and the light and stand is C$69.99 against C$59.97. Generic mats sell for C$17 to 24.
  • Big-ticket items hold their price. The Palram Hybrid 6 x 8 sells for C$1,249.99, against C$1,298 at Home Depot. Price pressure comes from cheaper models, such as an 8 x 6 at C$369.99 at Walmart. Competitors aren't selling the same model for less.
  • Pack sizes. Canadian Tire sells pellet refills only in packs of 36, at C$0.18 a pellet. Competitors sell counts of 72 and 200 at C$0.11 to 0.17 a pellet.
  • Room to grow in season extension. Other retailers sell frost cloth at C$10.99 to 28.99, cold frames at C$65 to 379, hoop kits at C$34 to 100 and heat mat thermostats at about C$40. Lee Valley carries all four.
Journey 2 - Snow, ice, leaves and storm debris: value in detailCanadian Tire is strongest on gas snowblowers and own-brand shovels. It has ground to make up against RONA on EGO, and on national-brand consumables. Some forum buyers pay the event price and treat the regular price as a reference.

Limits: we checked prices on 20 October 2026 on Home Depot, RONA, Walmart and Princess Auto pages. We compared them with Canadian Tire's regular prices in the Category Review. Amazon.ca blocked our reading and Costco showed no prices. Home Hardware prices did not load. Several competitor prices were temporary sales.

  • Gas snowblowers are the strongest value position. The YardForce 24 in sells for C$699.99, which is C$199 below Walmart's price for the same machine. The Champion 26 in, at C$1,199.99, sits 40% below the median for 26 to 30 in machines. Home Depot's PowerSmart 24 in (C$598) is the one machine priced below Canadian Tire's lowest. RONA's own-brand 24 in is C$799.
  • EGO matches RONA's regular price, and RONA discounts. The 16 in saw, the 24 and 28 in two-stage machines and the 12 in snow shovel carry the same regular price at both. On the day we checked, RONA showed them 7 to 12% lower. The EGO 765 CFM blower kit is C$469.99 at Canadian Tire and C$429 at RONA.
  • Own-brand 48V tools don't undercut rivals, except the snowblower. Yardworks sits above the median of similar kits by 15% on the blower, 24% on the pole saw and 13% on the 16 in saw. The Yardworks 48V 20 in snowblower kit sells for C$649.99, which is 35% below the median. The product list Canadian Tire shared doesn't give battery sizes for the other Yardworks kits, so battery size may explain part of the gap.
  • Same-brand consumables cost more at Canadian Tire. A 9 kg bag of Alaskan Premium is C$13.99 at Canadian Tire and C$10.98 at Walmart. A 20 kg bag of Sifto is C$8.99, against C$8.38 at Home Depot. Yardworks Ice Melter 20 kg works out to C$1.00/kg, the lowest price per kg of any premium melt we found.
  • For some forum buyers, the event price is the real price. In 27 comments, buyers time a purchase to Canadian Tire points events, such as 40x and 60x Triangle days that give about 16 to 24% back. In 73 comments, buyers talk about price matching. One buyer calls the regular price "slightly inflated". One reviewer praises how easy it is to get Certified parts at Canadian Tire.
Journey 3 - Pools and hot tubs: value in detailKits and accessories hold on price. Reviewers praise Canadian Tire's chemical prices. Branded equipment costs more than at the pool specialists. Spa-size chemicals cost more per kg than pool sizes do elsewhere. The core chemicals can't be compared yet.

These checks have limits. We checked prices on 20 October 2026 on Pool Supplies Canada, Pioneer, Walmart.ca, Home Depot and Costco pages. We compared them with Canadian Tire's regular prices in the Category Review. Home Depot and Costco showed no prices. The canadiantire.ca pages didn't load, so Canadian Tire prices come only from the Category Review.

  • Branded equipment costs more than at the specialists. The Aiper Scuba N1 is C$849.99 at Canadian Tire and C$599.97 at Pool Supplies Canada. The Steel Pro Max 15 ft pool is C$749.99 at Canadian Tire, against C$649. Some rival prices were sales. Even so, Pool Supplies Canada's regular N1 price of C$823.99 is still below Canadian Tire's.
  • We can't compare the core chemical basket. The product list Canadian Tire shared doesn't include trichlor pucks, shock, pool-size pH and alkalinity products, or algaecide. The canadiantire.ca site does list Aquarius and HTH pucks. Pool specialists charge C$8.33 to 12.50/kg for trichlor, C$15.53 to 17.60/kg for shock and C$5 to 7/kg for pH.
  • Spa sizes cost 2 to 3 times more per kg. Canadian Tire sells pH Plus at C$19.98/kg, while specialists sell a 2 kg pool size at C$7.00/kg. Hot tub bromine sits mid-market at C$37.99/kg.
  • Kits and accessories hold their ground. Aquarius opening and closing kits cost C$32.99 to 46.99, below rival kits at C$47.95 to 64.99. We haven't compared what's inside them. The Kokido Telsa 5 handheld vac costs C$99.99, the lowest price we found.
  • Walmart.ca is a marketplace, not a single low price. Its third-party sellers mark up specialist chemicals by 30 to 167%. Walmart.ca puts its real pressure on equipment. An Intex solar cover sells for C$54.98 against C$99.99, and inflatable spas start at C$469.99 against C$899.99.
  • Reviewers back the chemical prices. Canadian reviewers on canadiantire.ca say Canadian Tire's chemicals are fairly priced against local pool companies. They buy them on sale or on points days. Forum posters see Canadian Tire's low-cost solar blankets as one-season products.
What it meansPrice the repeat purchase as carefully as the first one.
  • Price refills and consumables. Where Canadian Tire owns the starter kit or the machine, bring refills, bags and spa-size chemicals in line with rivals. Larger packs with a clear per-unit price are another route.
  • Show the per-unit price. Yardworks Ice Melter 20 kg costs C$1.00/kg. Where own brand wins per kg like this, say so on the tag.
  • Use the event calendar deliberately. Some forum buyers wait for points events. Decide which products should anchor each event.
  • Branded equipment. Where the same model costs less at specialists, as with Aiper, price it to their regular price. The other route is to carry the models where Canadian Tire is competitive.

04 - Brands

Brand architecture across good, better, best

The question“Do we have the right brand architecture and assortment mix, and are our brands positioned appropriately across the Good-Better-Best spectrum?”
Executive summary

Own brand is strongest in manual snow tools, pool chemicals and parts, and national brands lead most powered equipment. Across 45 finelines, we make one own-brand recommendation for each.

12
finelines where own brand wins
keep it and promote it
8
openings for own brand
6 missing price levels and 2 new lines
20
finelines led by national brands
choose them well and price them right
5
own brands to bring home
sold elsewhere or under another name
WHERE OWN BRAND WINS
Yardworks, Aquarius and Certified carry the own-brand offer.
Yardworks runs good, better and best in snow pushers and scoops. Aquarius runs all three levels in pool water treatment. Certified is the entry level for snowblower belts, accessories and parts.
WHERE NATIONAL BRANDS LEAD
Products with a motor, a battery or a frame.
Own brand stops at the middle level in cordless tools. National brands lead gas snowblowers, gas saws, covers, robots and spas, and own brand has one pool, from Outbound.
WHAT TO BRING HOME
Some own brands that fit these journeys sit in other departments.
NOMA grow lights, the MAXIMUM compact blower and Mastercraft pumps all serve steps in these journeys. Shoppers meet them outside the Seasonal and Gardening offer, so the offer gets no credit for them.
How to read this tabEach fineline gets one of five recommendations, so the team can see where own brand should play.

This tab answers one question for each fineline: where should own brand play as the good, better, best offer takes shape? Each fineline gets one of five calls. Read the call first, then what the offer looks like today, the evidence behind it and the move for the buying or brand team.

These are our recommendations for the team to react to. Some price levels are our estimate from price, and we have no sales data. Price levels by product and sales by fineline from Canadian Tire would firm them up.

Journey 2Electric Chipper-ShreddersYardworks supplies the single electric shredder here, at the middle price level with a C$249.99 median.Own brand holds the fineline, and the pains are about leaves. 5 people say fall cleanup fills dozens of yard bags, and some shred leaves with a trimmer in a garbage can.Show leaf shredding on the Yardworks shredder box, signed 'fewer yard bags: shred leaves into bed mulch'.
Journey 2Electric Leaf Blowers & VacuumsYardworks and Certified hold 3 of 7 items across all three price levels, alongside Worx. Customers rate the Yardworks 400 CFM blower vac 4.28 from 280 ratings, and the Worx Trivac 4.07 from 879.Own brand has a real position in corded blower vacs, rated above the national rival. 18 people say leaf vacs have weak suction, and 10 say mulchers leave leaves nearly whole.Spec a metal impeller, wider intake and larger bag on the Yardworks blower vac, then show its rating at shelf.
Journey 2Electric SnowblowersCertified supplies both corded blowers here. Customers rate the Certified 13.5A 18 inch blower 4.04 from 418 ratings.Own brand holds the whole fineline, and customers rate it well. 19 people say extension cords get run over and stiffen in the cold, and 13 say small blowers struggle with as little as 5 cm.Show the Certified rating on the shelf tag, and pack a cold flexible cord with a lock in each box.
Journey 2Premium Ice MeltersYardworks holds 7 of 10 bags, at the opening and middle levels, with Alaskan at the middle. All 10 are made in Canada. Customers rate the Yardworks 10 kg bag 4.43 from 1611 ratings.The sourcing scan rates blended melters high for domestic supply. 12 people say melt seems slow or weaker than earlier bags, and 5 say it stops working near minus 7.Make the Yardworks 10 kg bag the storm endcap hero, and extend the line with a deep cold blend.
Journey 2Snow PushersYardworks holds 13 of 15 pushers across all three price levels, with Garant at the top. All 15 are made in Canada. Customers rate the Yardworks HD sleigh 4.71 from 615 ratings.Customers rate the range 4.46 from 1458 ratings, and the sourcing scan rates shovels high for domestic supply. 16 people say blades wobble at the handle joint, and 13 want an adjustable handle.Hero the Yardworks HD sleigh with its rating at the entrance, and extend the steel wear strip across every pusher.
Journey 2Snow ScoopsYardworks holds 8 of 9 scoops across all three price levels, from a C$19.99 median to C$47.99. All 9 are made in Canada.We didn't find pains tied to scoops in the comments. The sourcing scan rates snow shovels, pushers and scoops high for domestic supply.Keep Yardworks across all three price levels, and hold its Canadian supply.
Journey 2Specialty Snow ToolsYardworks holds 5 of 7 tools across all three price levels, with Garant at the middle and top. All 7 are made in Canada.Own brand leads, and most pains here are about technique. 9 people say packed snow refreezes into ice, and 7 say power shovels struggle with ice and heavy snow on decks.Extend Yardworks with a lighter deck shovel, and shelve the EasyHeat roof and gutter cable kit with the ice tools.
Journey 3Pool Closing KitsAquarius supplies all 3 closing kits, at the good and better levels, all made in Canada. Customers rate the Aquarius Quick Pool Closing Kit 4.66 from 126 ratings.Customers rate the kit highly, and 40 of 50 reviews read were positive. 9 people don't know which chemicals to add, and 5 say kits leave out antifreeze.Make the Quick Pool Closing Kit the fall display hero, and add main drain antifreeze to the kit.
Journey 3Pool Opening KitsAquarius supplies all 4 opening kits, at the good and better levels, all made in Canada. Customers rate the above ground kit 4.03 from 62 ratings.Own brand holds the fineline, and 21 of 35 reviews read on the kit are positive. 6 people don't know how to close and reopen so the pool opens clean.Feature the Aquarius kit on spring endcaps, and print the full opening sequence inside the box.
Journey 3Pool Replacement PartsAquarius and Outbound hold 18 of 38 items across all three price levels. Bestway, Intex and other national brands fill the rest, at the opening and middle levels.Own brand already holds every price level in parts. 13 people say replacement cartridges and bags are hard to find, and 5 say a failed liner means buying a new pool.Extend the own brand parts wall with Outbound replacement cartridges and liners, and Aquarius fine mesh filter socks.
Journey 3Pool Water TreatmentAquarius holds 25 of 40 items across all three price levels, alongside Aiper, GAME and Kokido. Customers rate the range 4.12 from 928 ratings, led by the Aiper Scuba 800 at 4.36.Own brand leads the chemicals and accessories. 34 people say test strip readings differ from other tests, and customers rate the Aquarius strips 3.97, so the strips are the place to protect the line.Keep Aquarius across all three levels, and reformulate its test strips to match the chart with a clear expiry date.
Journey 3Spa ChemicalsAquarius holds 17 of 18 items, all at the middle price level, alongside PharmaSpa. 11 are made in Canada. Customers rate the Aquarius bromine tablets 4.26 from 128 ratings.Own brand leads, and most pains are about dosing. 10 people don't know how much shock their tub needs, and 7 say sanitizer tablets crumble or dissolve too fast.Hero the Aquarius bromine tablets with their rating, and print shock dose by tub volume on each spa pack.
Own brand is here, but a price level is missing.Own brand is on the shelf but a price level is missing, and the pains or the national range show which one to add.
JourneyFinelineTodayWhy this callThe move
Journey 2Leaf RakesYardworks and Garden Club hold 9 of 11 rakes, at the opening and middle levels. Garant and Fiskars hold the top level, at a C$42.99 median. Customers rate the Yardworks 22 inch metal rake 3.74 from 203.7 people say tines and handles flex or bend under heavier material, and 4 say heads are too narrow. A sturdier, wider own brand rake would fill the top level.Add a Yardworks rake at the top price level with thicker tines, a stiffer handle and a wider head.
Journey 2ScrapersYardworks supplies both scrapers, at the opening and middle levels, with medians of C$21.99 and C$34.99. Both are made in China.10 people say plastic blades crack or wear down within a season, and 5 want replaceable wear strips. Those pains point to a tougher scraper at the top level.Add a Yardworks scraper at the top price level with a steel core handle and bolt on metal wear strips.
Journey 2Snowblower AccessoriesOwn brand holds 26 of 38 items, all Certified, at the opening price level. National brands such as Atlas and MTD fill the middle and top levels, with medians of C$69.99 and C$189.99.25 people say chutes and augers clog in wet snow, and 12 say snow freezes in the auger. 40 people turn to cooking spray, hot water or block heaters instead.Add Certified accessories at the middle price level, starting with a cold rated anti stick chute spray and a fitted cover.
Journey 2Snowblower BeltsOwn brand holds 32 of 42 belts, led by Certified, at the opening price level, with a C$29.99 median. National belts from Laser and MTD sit at the top level, at C$34.99.6 people say auger and drive belts slip off or snap, some within days. A heavier, cold rated belt would give own brand a middle level, which we didn't find in the range today.Add a heavier, cold rated Certified belt at the middle price level, with fit charts on the pack.
Journey 2Snowblower PartsOwn brand holds 24 of 50 items, led by Certified, at the opening price level. Laser, EGO and Greenworks parts hold the middle and top levels, with medians of C$24.99 and C$29.99.69 people say augers, chutes, belts and wheels break or loosen, often in early uses. That points to a tougher own brand part at the middle level. 17 can't find parts for working machines.Add Certified heavy duty parts at the middle level: steel augers, metal chute controls and universal fit shear pin packs.
Journey 3Pool Winterization EquipmentAquarius holds 4 of 7 items, all at the middle price level. Blue Wave and Bestway fill the opening and top levels, with a C$94.99 median at the top.9 people say snow on the winter cover strains walls and pushes water out, and 17 say skimmer plugs and air pillows don't fit or fail. Those pains point to a top level own brand kit.Add an Aquarius winter kit at the top price level, with a cover support system and skimmer plugs sized to common skimmers.
An opening for a new own-brand line.Own brand is absent here, people complain about failures or price, and the product is simple enough to source under an own brand.
JourneyFinelineTodayWhy this callThe move
Journey 1GreenhousesNational brands fill all 18 items, led by Palram and Shelter Logic, with medians of C$889.99 at the opening level and C$2,299.99 at the middle. Customers rate the range 4.01 from 246 ratings.41 people say kits buckle, rip or blow away, and 24 build cold frames and hoop houses from salvage. The sourcing scan rates walk in greenhouses and cold frames high for domestic supply.Develop an own brand walk in greenhouse and cold frame kit rated for Canadian snow loads, built with a Canadian maker such as Harnois.
Journey 3Pool CoversBestway supplies all 11 covers, at the opening and middle levels, with medians of C$41.99 and C$89.99. Customers rate the range 3.4 from 265 ratings. Own brand has no cover here.16 people say covers rip or wear through, 15 say they break down in sun, and 13 say they run small. The sourcing scan rates covers medium, with Canadian fabrication at Latham Kingston.Develop an Aquarius cover sized true to the pool, in UV stabilized material with welded seams and reinforced edges.
National brands lead here. Choose them well and price them right.National brands lead this product, so the work is choosing the right brands, pricing them against rivals and backing them with parts and support.
JourneyFinelineTodayWhy this callThe move
Journey 1Grow PotsPlanters' Pride supplies all 23 pots, at the opening and middle price levels, with medians of C$1.79 and C$6.99. Every pot is made in Canada or the US.The pains here are about technique, and we didn't find complaints about pots failing or their price. 13 people find potting up slow and don't know when to do it.Keep Planters' Pride, and add a shelf talker on when to pot up and how to hold a seedling.
Journey 1HydroponicsNational brands fill all 23 items, at the opening and middle price levels, with medians of C$29.99 and C$99.99. Customers rate the Jiffy Grow Light 4.41 from 82 ratings. Own brand has no light here.Grow lights are powered electronics, and the sourcing scan rates them low for domestic supply. 49 people want brighter, longer lasting lights at fair prices, and 18 say brackets and stands break or won't fit.Ask suppliers for wider white lights with replaceable tubes and adjustable stands, and hold steady everyday prices against online rivals.
Journey 1Indoor WateringPanacea and Bloem fill the 9 items across all three price levels, with medians from C$9.99 to C$26.99. Own brand has no watering line here.The pains here are about technique. 6 people don't know how much or how often to water new seedlings, and we didn't find complaints about the cans failing.Keep the national range, and tag each watering product with plain seedling advice: water from below and let the surface dry.
Journey 1Seed Starting MixesFive national mixes fill this fineline, all made in Canada. The opening and top price levels share a C$10.99 median. Customers rate the leading mix 4.35 from 247 ratings.Customers rate the leading mix well, and the sourcing scan finds peat mixes already made in Canada. 5 people say mixes dry out fast, and 5 find them overpriced.Ask the vendor for a finer, moisture holding mix in a larger value bag, and set the two price levels apart.
Journey 1Seeds and Seed KitsMcKenzie and other seed brands fill all 24 items, at the middle and top price levels. All 24 are made in Canada. Own brand has no seed line here.Seeds are a brand and variety choice, and the pains here are about timing. 11 people can't tell which crops to start indoors or sow direct. The middle level median of C$12.99 sits above the top level at C$10.49.Fix the seed price ladder with McKenzie, and add early maturing pepper and tomato varieties under a short season sign.
Journey 2Chainsaw AccessoriesOregon, Husqvarna and EGO fill the 23 items at the middle and top price levels. 11 are made in the US. Own brand has no accessories here.Sharpening tools follow the chain brands. 7 people don't know how to grind chains, and 5 say saws come without bar oil, so new owners can't cut on day one.Shelve bar oil beside every saw, and post a chain to file size chart at the sharpening shelf.
Journey 2Chainsaw Chains & BarsOregon leads the 57 items, with EGO, Husqvarna and Worx, at the middle and top price levels. 27 items are made in Canada or the US. Own brand has no chains here.Chains and bars must fit specific saws, so the brand carries the trust. 16 people want tensioners that hold, and 6 swap stock chains for Oregon or Stihl.Sign Oregon chains as the upgrade for stock chains, and stock metal tensioner kits for Yardworks and EGO saws.
Journey 2Cordless ChainsawsWorx, EGO and Greenworks lead the 27 saws. Yardworks and Mastercraft hold 4 at the middle price level, with a C$199.99 median. Customers rate the EGO 18 inch saw 4.65 from 2386 ratings.Battery saws ride on platforms, and own brand would struggle to earn trust at the top. 24 people say packs last 30 to 45 minutes, and 15 say saws bog on thicker wood.Make the EGO 18 inch saw the storm cleanup hero, and bundle a second large battery with the top saws.
Journey 2Cordless Leaf Blowers & VacuumsEGO, Greenworks and Worx lead the 32 items. Own brand holds 6, at the opening and middle levels. Customers rate the EGO 765 CFM blower 4.59 from 4297 ratings.The battery platform drives this choice. 26 people keep a gas blower for big jobs, 24 say packs run down before the job is done, and 13 say rivals refuse price matches.Hero the EGO 765 CFM blower, and source a cordless leaf vacuum on each battery platform carried.
Journey 2Cordless PolesawsGreenworks, Worx and EGO lead the 11 saws. Mastercraft and Yardworks hold 2 at the middle price level, with a C$249.99 median against C$399.99 at the top.Pole saws ride on battery platforms. 9 people say extended pole saws are heavy and tiring, and 5 say batteries run down in minutes or falter in the cold.Choose national pole saws with lighter shafts and larger batteries, and print a safe high cut guide on each pack.
Journey 2Cordless SnowblowersEGO, Greenworks and Worx lead the 33 machines, with a top level median of C$1,199.99. Yardworks and Mastercraft hold 5, at the opening and middle levels. Customers rate the EGO two stage 4.48 from 2344 ratings.Battery platforms decide the brand, and the sourcing scan rates cordless tools low for domestic supply. 49 people say spare batteries cost hundreds of dollars, and 45 say blowers bog in wet snow.Lead with the EGO self propelled two stage, bundle a second battery in kits, and publish one clear price match policy.
Journey 2Gas ChainsawsHusqvarna leads the 6 saws, at the middle and top price levels. Customers rate the Husqvarna 38cc 16 inch saw 4.11 from 679 ratings. Own brand has no gas saw here.Gas saws are engine products, and own brand has no position here. 5 people say gas saws are hard to pull start, and 5 say rarely used saws need carb work.Pair each gas saw with ethanol free fuel and bar oil, and add an easy start model.
Journey 2Gas Leaf Blowers & VacuumsHusqvarna supplies the single gas backpack blower, at the top price level with a C$469.99 median. Customers rate it 4.41 from 993 ratings.Gas blowers are engine products led by a trusted brand. 8 people say battery blowers clear only light snow, and 6 say gas blowers are loud.Feature the Husqvarna backpack as the big yard hero, and source a quieter gas model with its noise rating shown.
Journey 2Gas SnowblowersBriggs & Stratton, Toro and other national brands fill all 14 machines, at the opening and top levels, with medians of C$1,199.99 and C$1,999.99. Customers rate the Briggs & Stratton 24 inch two stage 3.15 from 115.Gas machines rely on engines, dealers and parts, and own brand has no position here. 82 people want a durable, easy starting machine at a fair price, and 19 can't judge a deal.Bring in a compact two stage model with electric start and stocked parts, and post a driveway size selector at shelf.
Journey 2Leaf Blower AccessoriesWorx and Greenworks supply the 3 items at the middle price level, with a C$69.99 median. Own brand has no blower accessories here.Accessories have to fit a blower platform. 7 people say blow tubes come in one length, and 3 say gutter kits get heavy overhead and fall short.Source extension and short blow tubes for core platforms, and list which blowers each gutter kit fits.
Journey 2Rock SaltSifto supplies both bags here, at the middle level with a C$8.99 median, made in Canada. Customers rate the Sifto 20 kg bag 4.34 from 438 ratings.Sifto is a trusted Canadian name at a low price, and the sourcing scan finds rock salt already domestic. 7 people say granules spread unevenly, and 5 couldn't get salt during shortages.Pre book extra Sifto pallets before storm season, and agree a tighter grain size and a clean salt check.
Journey 3Simple-set PoolsFUNSICLE supplies all 3 pools here, at the opening price level, with a C$129.99 median. Own brand has no pool here.Budget pools are labour heavy imports, and the sourcing scan rates them low for domestic supply. 6 people see them as single season buys.Ask FUNSICLE for a thicker liner, and print the expected seasons of use on the box.
Journey 3Spa Replacement PartsExcel, Salu Spa and other national brands lead the 31 items across all three levels. Aquarius holds 6 at the opening and middle levels. Customers rate the Salu Spa Thermal Spa Cover 4.73 from 220 ratings.Spa parts must fit specific tubs, so the tub brands carry the trust. 6 people say inflatable tub filters clog within days, and 5 say pumps, heaters and jets wear out within a few years.Make the Salu Spa thermal cover the add on at every spa sale, and ask Excel for longer life parts.
Journey 3SpasSalu Spa, Canadian Spa Company and Coleman fill the 6 tubs, at the middle and top levels, with medians of C$1,099.99 and C$1,999.99. Own brand has no tub here.Tubs need service and warranties that hold. 8 people say big box tubs lack local service, and 8 say warranties protect less than expected. The sourcing scan rates Canadian hard sided tubs high.Widen the hard sided range with a Canadian maker such as Arctic Spas or Hydropool, backed by local service.
Journey 3Steel Frame PoolsColeman, Intex and other national brands fill 11 of 12 pools across all three levels. The Outbound pool is the one own brand option, at the middle level. Customers rate the fineline 3.36.Frame pools are complex kits, and the sourcing scan rates them low for domestic supply. 7 people say bundled pumps are too small, and 6 say legs sink and the frame buckles.Choose frame pools with metal connectors and wide leg footings, and bundle a larger filter pump with each kit.
An own brand that fits is sold elsewhere or under another name.Canadian Tire already sells an own brand that fits this step elsewhere or under another name, so the move is to bring it into Seasonal and Gardening.

Journey 1NOMA grow lights (outside Seasonal and Gardening)NOMA grow bulbs and T5 strips sit in another department, outside Seasonal and Gardening. Three of the four products carry 77 to 137 reviews at 4.4 to 4.6 stars.Customers rate NOMA strips and bulbs well, and the grow light bay has no own brand. 18 people report lights failing early, with NOMA named most, so the move needs testing.Bring NOMA T5 strips and grow bulbs into the seed starting bay, with burn in testing and an adjustable hanging kit.
Journey 1Seed StartingJiffy and McKenzie lead the 19 items across all three price levels. The two Garden Club items, a tray and a dome at the middle level, carry the Jiffy name on canadiantire.ca.Shoppers can't see the own brand they already buy. 76 people want rigid trays, fitted domes and reliable heat mats, and 14 say trays crack or buckle when full.Sell the Garden Club tray and dome under the Garden Club name, built heavier and with domes that seat firmly.
Journey 2MAXIMUM compact blower (outside Seasonal and Gardening)The MAXIMUM compact blower sits in the tools department on canadiantire.ca, outside Seasonal and Gardening. It serves the gutter cleaning step, where Worx and Greenworks supply the blower accessories.MAXIMUM is an own brand that already fits this step. 3 people say blowers can't shift wet gutter debris or reach far sections, and the accessories here carry no own brand.Show the MAXIMUM compact blower beside the gutter and blower accessories, online and in store.
Journey 2Yardworks PawProtect ice melt (outside Seasonal and Gardening)Yardworks PawProtect pet friendly ice melt is on canadiantire.ca, outside the product list Canadian Tire shared. Yardworks and Alaskan fill the premium melt range.Yardworks already makes a pet friendly melt, and customers rate the core Yardworks bag 4.43 from 1611 ratings. 5 people say melt residue damages what it touches.Bring Yardworks PawProtect into the premium melt range, shelved beside the 10 kg bag as the pet friendly choice.
Journey 3Mastercraft pumps (outside Seasonal and Gardening)The Mastercraft 1/2 HP pool pump kit and Mastercraft utility pumps sit outside the pool range. Bestway supplies the pumps inside it, and kit pools ship with their own small pumps.14 people say filter pumps last a season or less, and 7 say pumps bundled with pools are too small. 44 people are unsure how to drain and winterize the pool.Offer the Mastercraft 1/2 HP kit as the upgrade at the pool and parts wall, and shelve utility pumps with winter gear.
Assortment mix: where the range is deep and where the need isThe range is deepest in parts, chain care and hot tub upkeep, and thinnest where people struggle most: choosing a snowblower, fixing breakdowns, liners, testing and grow lights.

For each sub-step, this compares the share of the journey’s products that serve it with the share of the people raising pain points there. A product can serve more than one sub-step, so the shares show where the range leans rather than an exact count.

  • Journey 1. Grow lights and seed-starting supplies carry 9% and 11% of the people raising pains, and 4% and 7% of the products. The range leans toward seeds, pellets and pots, where far fewer people raise problems.
  • Journey 2. Choosing a snowblower carries 22% of the people raising pains and 6% of the products, and fixing breakdowns carries 13% against 6%. Replacement parts and chain care hold 28% of the products and 7% of the pain.
  • Journey 3. Repairing leaks and liners carries 9% of the people raising pains and two products. Testing the water and choosing chemicals carry 6% each, against 2% of the products. The range leans toward hot tub upkeep and choosing a pool.

Journey 1 - Start earlier, protect longer: brands in detailOwn brand appears in one of the journey's seven finelines, at a single tier. Customers see it under the Jiffy name. NOMA holds the strongest own-brand position in the journey, and it sits outside the product list Canadian Tire shared.

Limits: the brand placement list Canadian Tire shared gives tiers by brand within each fineline. Where a brand holds several tiers, we split its products across them in price order and marked those tiers as estimates. A tier for each product would confirm them.

  • One own-brand position. Garden Club makes a seed tray with a dome at the better tier, and canadiantire.ca lists it under the Jiffy name. The good and best tiers are open for own brand across the journey.
  • NOMA grow lights are Canadian Tire's own brand, and customers rate the bulbs and T5 strips 4.4 to 4.6 stars on 77 to 137 reviews each. They're sold outside Seasonal and Gardening.
  • Grow lights come from one supplier. SunBlaster and Jump Start are both Hydrofarm brands.
  • Tiers that don't follow price. Better seed packets cost more than best ones, at medians of C$12.99 and C$10.49. Good and best seed-starting mix share a C$10.99 median. Canadian Tire carries one heat mat, at the best tier, for C$44.99.
  • Tiers mix product types. In greenhouses, the good tier holds walk-ins at a C$785 median. The better tier includes C$60 mini greenhouses. Read the ladder by product type.
Journey 2 - Snow, ice, leaves and storm debris: brands in detailOwn brand holds the entry and middle of manual snow tools, and it is also the parts brand. In powered tools it reaches the better tier. Gas machines have no own brand.

Limits: the brand placement list Canadian Tire shared gives tiers by brand within each fineline. Where a brand holds several tiers, we split its products across them in price order and marked those tiers as estimates. They cover 33% of the products in this journey. A tier for each product would firm this up. We treat MAXIMUM as own brand.

  • Manual snow tools. Yardworks covers good, better and best in pushers, scoops and specialty tools. Garant, a national brand, sits at best only.
  • Parts. Certified is the good tier in snowblower belts (32 of 42), accessories (26 of 38) and parts (24 of 50). National parts brands (Laser, MTD, EGO, Greenworks) sit at better and best.
  • Powered tools stop at better. Yardworks and Mastercraft hold the better tier in cordless snowblowers, leaf blowers, chainsaws and pole saws. National brands hold all of best: EGO, Greenworks and Worx.
  • Own brand is absent from gas snowblowers (Briggs & Stratton, Toro), gas chainsaws (Husqvarna), gas chipper-shredders, and chains and bars (Oregon).
  • Ice melt. Yardworks covers good and better, and Alaskan sits at better. Yardworks PawProtect is sold on canadiantire.ca but isn't in the product list Canadian Tire shared.
  • Battery platforms decide the brand. The platform a buyer picks for the snowblower decides the blower and saw that follow. Owners also worry that a platform will be dropped.
Journey 3 - Pools and hot tubs: brands in detailAquarius is the chemicals and accessories brand. It runs all three tiers in pool water treatment. Own brand has room to grow in equipment, where it has one pool and no covers, robots or spas.

We set the tier by price within a brand for 56% of the products in this journey, so those tiers are our estimate. Treat the tier pattern as a guide until Canadian Tire confirms the tier for each product. Aiper has no brand listed in the product list Canadian Tire shared. We count it as a national brand.

  • Aquarius covers good, better and best in pool water treatment, with 25 of 40 products. All 17 own-brand spa chemicals sit in the better tier. Aquarius also covers opening and closing kits and winterizing gear.
  • One own-brand pool. The Outbound steel frame pool sits in the better tier. Reviewers give it 2.6 stars, the lowest in the journey's reviews, and mention seam leaks. Coleman, Intex, Hydro-Force and Bestway supply the rest of the pools.
  • No own brand yet. Pool covers come from Bestway, robotic cleaners from Aiper, spas from SaluSpa, Canadian Spa Company and Coleman, and spa filters from Excel.
  • Chlorine and shock are missing from the Category Review. Canadian Tire lists 21 Aquarius and HTH puck and shock products on canadiantire.ca. We need to place them before we can finish Q1 and Q2 for chemicals.
05 - Sourcing

Domestic manufacturing and sourcing

The question“Are there any whitespace opportunities or priority categories where domestic manufacturing is particularly strong and could present additional development potential?”
Executive summary

Bulky, simple products where freight is a large share of the cost make the strongest domestic options: shovels and ice melt, frost cloth and cold frames, pool balancers and hard-sided hot tubs. Cordless tools, robots and frame pools are shifting from one Asian country to another.

65%
of Journey 1 SKUs made in Canada or the US
mostly peat and seed
27%
of Journey 2 SKUs
own-brand shovels and ice melt, and US-made Oregon chain
15%
of Journey 3 SKUs
mostly Aquarius chemicals and kits
8
sourcing bets
where a domestic option meets an open need
THE BEST BETS
Where domestic supply meets an open need.
Frost cloth and cold frames would be new to the range. Own-brand shovels and packaged ice melt are already made domestically. Balancers come only in spa sizes in the Category Review. One hard-sided hot tub is in the range.
THE HARD ONES
Electronics, batteries and PVC, plus test strips.
Cordless tools and platforms, robots and steel-frame pools rate low as supply moves from China to Vietnam and other Asian countries. Test strips rate low because US makers already serve the market.
THE CAVEAT
Trade measures change fast.
Trade measures dated after mid 2026 come from desk research. A broker should check them before anyone builds a business case.
Sourcing bets: domestic options that meet an open needThese product types rate high for domestic supply. Each one sits where the journey shows a gap, a product to fix or a need to say it better.

Domestic ratings by product type, all journeysHigh means a credible Canadian or US supply base and a freight or tariff case. Low means a new domestic maker has little room, because supply is moving within Asia or incumbents already serve the market.
JourneyProduct typeDomestic whitespaceWhat the rating rests on
Journey 1Frost cloth and row coverHighSpunbond fabric is made in North Bay, Ontario. Cutting and packing for retail needs little capital.
Journey 1Cold frames and hoop kitsHighThese are long, awkward metal kits. Their inputs are domestic, and no Canadian retail brand is on the shelf.
Journey 1Walk-in polycarbonate greenhousesHighThese are bulky to ship. Canada has aluminium and builders, such as BC Greenhouse Builders and Harnois.
Journey 1Trays, inserts and domesMediumUS makers produce these at scale. Trays nest, which weakens the case for saving on freight.
Journey 1Fibre and moulded-pulp potsMediumPeat pots are already made in Canada. Moulded pulp uses local recycled fibre.
Journey 1Heat mats and thermostatsMediumCertification is a barrier for importers. A Québec heating maker exists.
Journey 1Synthetic shrub coversMediumThese are imported today. They could use Ontario fabric, but sewing labour offsets the freight saving.
Journey 1Peat pellets and mixesLow (already domestic)Peat is Canadian already. Coir comes from India and Sri Lanka.
Journey 1LED grow lightsLowSupply is moving from China to Southeast Asia. North America isn't picking it up.
Journey 1Mini greenhousesLowThese are low cost, compact kits with sewn covers that take a lot of labour.
Journey 2Cordless outdoor power equipment and battery platformsLowCells, electronics and platforms are made in China. Chervon and Greenworks are moving this work to Vietnam. In North America, US assembly is limited to platform owners like STIHL.
Journey 2Gas two-stage snowblowers, gas chainsawsMediumThe US has a real manufacturing base: Ariens in Brillion, Toro in Windom and STIHL in Virginia. Section 232 tariffs favour US chainsaws. Stanley Black & Decker is exiting some gas lines. Canada has no assembler, and engines are imported.
Journey 2Chipper-shreddersMediumWallenstein, a Canadian fabricator in St. Clements, Ontario, already builds them. Volumes are low and the units are bulky. Engines are imported, and we haven't verified where Canadian Tire's current range is made.
Journey 2Snow shovels, pushers, scoopsHighGarant makes more than 4M tools a year in Québec. Its parent, AMES, is shifting toward China. These tools are bulky and cheap, and the tooling costs little. Canadian counter-tariffs penalize US-made tools.
Journey 2Ice melters and rock saltHighCanada and the US make rock salt and all chloride inputs, at Goderich, Windsor, Ludington and Slave Lake. Blending and bagging near distribution centres needs little capital. Freight costs are high against the value of the product.
Journey 2Leaf rakes and leaf bagsHigh for bags, medium for rakesPaper leaf bags are bulky and cheap, and they're made from domestic kraft paper. Ontario already has a converter. Canada's 50% counter-tariff on US paper favours converting in Canada.
Journey 2Replacement partsMediumChain and bar makers already run plants in Guelph and Virginia Beach. Job shops could make pins and augers. OEM part numbers and small volumes limit that opening.
Journey 3Chlorine and sanitizersMedium for tableting and packing, low for activesUS capacity for actives shrank when Conyers closed. Canada has no producer. A PMRA-registered Canadian tableter is plausible, though actives stay imported. Class 5.1 dangerous goods rules apply.
Journey 3Balancers and specialty chemicalsHighUS plants make bicarbonate, bisulfate and calcium chloride from domestic inputs. Blending needs little capital and mostly needs no registration. The product is heavy, which suits local packing.
Journey 3Test strips and kitsLowHach (Elkhart), LaMotte and Taylor already make them in the US. The product is light, so freight gives a new Canadian plant no advantage.
Journey 3Pumps and sand/cartridge filtersMediumNorth America already has a base, with Hayward in Nashville, Waterway in Oxnard and Carvin in Saint-Hyacinthe. Hayward is cutting China's share of its cost of goods from 10% to 3%. Entry-level combos stay in Asia. Efficiency and CSA rules favour incumbents.
Journey 3Robotic and suction cleanersLowChinese brands lead this consumer electronics category and are now moving to Vietnam, as the Aiper ruling of June 2026 shows. Maytronics is consolidating in Israel.
Journey 3Winter and solar coversMediumBoth countries have proven fabricators, including GLI in Youngstown, Latham in Kingston and Midwest Canvas. Covers are bulky. We haven't verified where the film and scrim come from.
Journey 3Steel-frame and inflatable poolsLowBestway will make every category in Vietnam by March 2027. The product is labour-heavy PVC. The domestic opening is in the adjacent category of steel-wall pools, made by Trévi in Mirabel.
Journey 3Hot tubs and spa partsHigh (hard-sided)Several Canadian makers build tubs, including Arctic Spas in Alberta, Hydropool in Ontario, and Coast and Beachcomber in BC. Tubs are costly to ship. Section 338 puts their US exports at risk and may free capacity for Canadian Tire.
Trade measures behind the ratingsThese measures shape the domestic case. Several are dated after mid 2026 and need checking with a customs broker.
MeasureWhat it doesDateRelevance
US IEEPA tariffs struck downThe Supreme Court held that IEEPA does not allow tariffs. Collection stopped for entries from Feb 24, 2026Ruling Feb 20, 2026The 2025 "reciprocal" and fentanyl tariffs are gone. Chervon reported receiving tariff refunds in H1 2026
US Section 122A global surcharge of 10%, then 15%, with USMCA goods exemptFeb 24 to Jul 24, 2026 (expired)Gone
US Section 301 "forced labour" tariffs12.5% on China and Vietnam, and 10% on India, Mexico and Canada. USMCA-qualifying goods are exempt. The tariff stacks on the existing China 301 tariffs.From Jul 24, 2026New baseline on most Asian imports into the US
US Section 301 (China, 2024 four-year review)Lithium-ion non-EV batteries rise from 7.5% to 25%Jan 1, 2026Cordless OPE batteries from China
US Section 232 steel and aluminum derivatives50% on steel and aluminum content. The list adds 407 codes, including chain saws (8467.22, 8467.81), other handheld tools (8467.29), mowers (8433.xx), certain pumps (8413.81) and parts, filters (8421.29) and 9506.91. It leaves out shovels and rakes (8201), snowblowers (8430.20), 8436.80 and saw chain (8202.40).Effective Aug 18, 2025Favours US assembly of chainsaws and some pumps
US Section 338 on Canada50% on specified Canadian goods, with no USMCA exemption. The lists include wood products, some machinery, plastics and plastic articles, "toys and sporting equipment" including pools, and base-metal goods such as toolsEffective Aug 22, 2026 (announced Jul 20)Affects Canadian makers who export to the US. We have not confirmed whether it covers hot tubs, shovels or outdoor power equipment.
Canada's counter-tariffs on US goodsC$27.6B in counter-tariffs at 15, 25 or 50%. Plastics and polymers 50%; hand tools and cutlery 15 to 25%; machinery and appliances 15 to 50%. Steel, aluminum and steel derivative surtaxes raised to 50%.Effective Sep 8, 2026Raises the cost of US made goods coming into Canada, which favours Canadian makers. The Finance Canada item list was not available, so coverage of codes 8201, 8430.20, 3922, 9506 and 8413, pool chemicals and salt is not confirmed.
Canada's steel tariff rate quotas and surtaxesA 50% surtax applies to steel mill products over quota. The quota for countries without a free trade agreement drops to 20% of 2024 levels from Dec 26, 2025. A 25% surtax applies to Chinese melt and pour steel from Jul 31, 2025. A 25% surtax applies to steel derivatives from all countries from Dec 26, 2025. It covers wire articles, 7308 structures, 7318 fasteners and 7314 mesh, and leaves out shovels, pools and Ch. 84 machinery.2025Raises the cost of steel for Canadian makers
US de minimis endedThe $800 exemption is suspended for all countries. The Court of International Trade upheld the suspension on Aug 13, 2026, and the statute repeals it on Jul 1, 2027.From Aug 29, 2025Ends duty free shipping from China direct to US consumers, for goods such as robots, test strips and small parts
Journey 1 - Start earlier, protect longer: sourcing in detailThe strongest domestic options in this journey are bulky outdoor gear: frost cloth and row cover, cold frames and hoop kits, and walk-in greenhouses. Indoor electronics and coir favour overseas supply.

In Journey 1, 65% of products are made in Canada or the US. The share is high because peat and seed products are Canadian. Every greenhouse in the range is imported.

Limits: this is a desk scan, with sources in the Method tab. A broker should check customs codes and any trade measures dated after mid 2026 before any business case.

Journey 2 - Snow, ice, leaves and storm debris: sourcing in detailBulky, simple products make the strongest domestic options: shovels and pushers, ice melt and salt, and paper leaf bags. Production of powered tools and batteries is moving within Asia. North America isn't picking it up.

In Journey 2, 27% of products are made in Canada or the US. Most of the Canadian share is own-brand, manual product. That includes snow pushers (13 of 15 own brand, made in Canada), scoops (8 of 9), specialty snow tools (5 of 7) and ice melters (7 of 10). The US share is mostly Oregon chains and accessories.

Limits: this is a desk scan. A customs broker should check trade measures dated after mid 2026, and the customs codes, before any business case.

Journey 3 - Pools and hot tubs: sourcing in detailBalancers and specialty chemicals are the strongest domestic options, along with hard-sided hot tubs from Canadian makers. Pools, robots and test strips favour overseas or existing US supply.

In Journey 3, 15% of products are made in Canada or the US. Most of these are own-brand chemicals, 20 of 27. They include spa chemicals made in Canada (10 of 17 own brand), 4 opening kits and 3 closing kits. The Canadian Spa Company hard-sided spa also counts. Pools, pumps, filters, covers and robots are imported, mainly from China.

Limits: this is a desk scan. A customs broker should check trade measures dated after mid 2026, and the customs codes, before any business case.

07 - Method

How we did the research

Executive summary

We coded 22,972 comments from Reddit, RedFlagDeals, YouTube and canadiantire.ca reviews to the steps of each job and grouped them into distinct pain points, hacks and fineline opportunities, all secondary research ready to test with customers.

Sources by journeyReader agents coded four kinds of source. Every quote is checked word for word against the saved pages.
JourneyRedditRedFlagDealsYouTube commentsYouTube captionscanadiantire.ca reviewsTotalFrom Canada
Journey 1 - Start earlier, protect longer1,7184291,1342281,1124,62143%
Journey 2 - Snow, ice, leaves and storm debris2,8884,0312,64202,27811,83963%
Journey 3 - Pools and hot tubs2,1711,3251,03501,9816,51253%
How the map is builtEach comment is coded to a job, a stage, a step and a sub-step, with its sentiment and themes.
  • Steps and sub-steps. Each journey runs through eight stages (Define, Locate, Prepare, Confirm, Execute, Monitor, Modify, Conclude), with steps and sub-steps drawn from what people describe doing.
  • Complaint share. This is the share of comments that are negative, with a mixed comment counted as half.
  • Pain points. We kept every distinct problem raised by at least 5 people at a sub-step, or 3 in small sub-steps, and questions people ask count too. One person repeating a point counts once. We then re-read every card against the full text of each comment it cites. We removed comments that did not express the problem, cut wording back to what people said, merged duplicates and dropped cards that fell below the threshold. Each card is tagged as product fails, missing product, knowledge gap or price.
  • Hacks. A hack is a homemade workaround raised by at least 3 people. It is what people rig instead of buying.
  • Finelines. We matched products from the Category Review and canadiantire.ca to sub-steps by product type. Each fineline shows own brand and competitive counts, good, better and best tiers, and canadiantire.ca ratings.
  • Fineline opportunities. We placed each pain and hack once. A gap is something to source or create. A fix means the fineline falls short of the need. Say it better means Canadian Tire sells the answer and customers don't know it. Speak louder means a rating of 4.2 or higher on 50 or more ratings, or 60% positive on 20 or more reviews read.
  • Territories. A territory is a distinct customer outcome, and no two territories share a sub-step. Each one covers struggles, what Canadian Tire sells today, price against the market and moves by team.
  • Checks. Quotes are checked word for word against the saved pages. We count from the comments themselves, and agents do not supply the counts. A separate agent fact checks each journey's copy before it goes in the brief.
What the numbers can and can't tell youCounts show that a problem exists and how often people raised it in what we read. They are not market shares.
  • Canadian share. Canadians wrote 56% of the comments. The rest come from benchmark markets, mostly the US, or from unknown locations.
  • The deals forum. RedFlagDeals is the best Canadian source we found. It tilts the value evidence toward sale timing, points events and price matching.
  • Reviews. We kept canadiantire.ca reviews copied from brand sites, and incentivized reviews, but weighted them lower. Home Depot Canada reviews did not load.
  • No sales data. Speak-louder opportunities rest on ratings and reviews. Sales by fineline would confirm them and let the ranking weigh revenue.
  • Tiers. Some good, better and best tiers are our estimate from price within a brand.
  • Trade measures. Measures dated after mid 2026 come from desk research and need a broker's check.
